title: The HTTP server has zero tests; /api/source serves arbitrary files and /api/analyze runs git clone on unvalidated input
evidence: The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32). /api/source reads the decoded `file` query verbatim as a path (109-124, 200-205), so `?file=/etc/passwd` or `..%2F..%2F` paths return file contents. /api/analyze passes repo_url straight to `git clone` (429-437). WebRepoFetcher::validate_url is never called, its only test is the happy path, and it panics on `https://github.com/owner` because of `parts[1]` (web_repo.rs:111-112). A failed clone silently analyses the first directory in target_repos and still reports success (467-482). Error JSON is interpolated unescaped (530-533). No test touches any route.
impact: Any network peer can read files readable by the server user. Results can silently come from the wrong repository, and unescaped error text produces invalid JSON. No regression net exists.
recommendation: Refactor routing into a pure `fn handle(req: &[u8], ctx: &Ctx) -> Response` and add table-driven tests. Traversal payloads (absolute, `..`, `%2e%2e`, `C:\\`) must return 403/404. repo_url must match ^https://github.com/[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+$ and never start with `-`. A failed clone must return an error, and every response body must parse with serde_json. Add a cargo-fuzz or proptest target over arbitrary request bytes (no panics), plus an integration test on 127.0.0.1:0. Bind 127.0.0.1 by default.

title: Every non-Java language is parsed with a foreign grammar, silently
evidence: Cargo.toml:8-10 ships only tree-sitter-java and tree-sitter-javascript. src/ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31 returns `tree_sitter_java::language()`, yet its map targets tree-sitter-kotlin kinds that the Java grammar never emits ('simple_identifier', '?:', '!!' at :35,57). Both registries fall back to a JavaScript-grammar adapter for any unregistered LangId (src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39,56; src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:20-28,41). The AST registry has no Kotlin entry, so a .kt file is lexed as Java in Phase 1 and re-parsed as JavaScript in Phase 2 (src/ast/mod.rs:141-143). Python, TS, Rust, C++, Go, Swift, C# and the server's extra extensions (.sh, .sql, .asm; src/adapters/server.rs:805-866) all become JavaScript. Nothing in src/ calls has_error or is_missing.
impact: For every advertised non-Java language the parse tree is mostly ERROR nodes. Symbols, CFGs, SSA, the call graph and all diagrams are therefore artifacts of mis-parsing; for Kotlin, tokens and AST even come from two different grammars. Users get no warning.
recommendation: Ship real grammars (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng, -python, -typescript/tsx, -rust, -cpp, -go) after moving to tree-sitter 0.24+. Put them behind one registry with no JavaScript fallback; unsupported files are skipped with a diagnostic. Record per-file ERROR/MISSING node ratios (Node::has_error, Node::is_missing) in the .tca file record and the API response, and flag or exclude files above a threshold. Done = a per-language conformance corpus that parses with zero ERROR nodes, asserted in CI.

title: Kotlin token heuristics run on every file and invent members and inheritance, including in Java
evidence: src/symbol/passes/pass1_discovery.rs:200-456 ('Secondary Token-Level Discovery Sweep for Kotlin & Multi-Lang') never checks the language. After any fun/val/var token, the next alphabetic token within 10 becomes a member of current_class_sym (:414-453); there is no scope check and no per-file reset (:257). src/symbol/passes/pass5_hierarchy.rs:76-157 treats any ':' or 'extends' before '{' as a supertype. A Python port of both loops (C:/Users/AHMAD_~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--Repos-OpenHeart/31873741-1e3a-46df-bb5d-a94a867cbe24/scratchpad/lens/sweep_sim.py) produces these results. Java `var sum` and `int val = compute()` give fields sum and compute; `@Import({Repo.class, Mailer.class})` gives a phantom class Mailer. Kotlin local vals become fields, `fun <T>` gives a method T, and `fun String.shout` gives a method String. `Repo<T extends BaseEntity>` and `data class Order(val c: Customer)` give bogus extends edges. The CLI also feeds build.gradle.kts files to the sweep (src/main.rs:79-93).
impact: Modern Java code (`var` since Java 10, generic bounds) and nearly every Kotlin file get phantom fields and methods and false generalizations in class, package and pattern output. The name-only F1 harness cannot see phantom members or duplicate classes.
recommendation: Delete the sweeps and derive Kotlin declarations from tree-sitter-kotlin-ng through a real lowering. Interim steps: run each heuristic only when the file's language is Kotlin (tca.file_records[fid].language_id); track brace depth to reset current_class_sym per file and at depth 0; skip type-parameter and constructor-parameter lists in Pass 5; and set first_token_id on sweep-created symbols (pass1_discovery.rs:439-446) so Pass 4 (pass4_members.rs:60-71) can give them types. Add the snippets above as regression fixtures.

title: Phase 8 longest-path DFS enumerates every CFG path: exponential hang on ordinary methods
evidence: psa/construction/mod.rs:153-173 compute_max_path_length pops (block, depth) and pushes every successor with depth+1 (line 168), with no visited or memo set. The only cut is depth >= bound, where bound = block count (158), and acyclic paths never reach it. It runs for every function (mod.rs:116, via psa/mod.rs:129). A Python model of if_stmt.rs block shapes (scratchpad lens/scale_model.py) costs exactly 4·2^k pops for k sequential ifs: k=22 gives 16.8M pops and k=40 gives 4.4·10^12. Loops turn it into walk enumeration up to length n.
impact: Any method with roughly 35+ independent branches (serializers, toXContent, validators) never finishes Phase 8, so the CLI run and the server request hang. Remotely triggerable through POST /api/analyze.
recommendation: Replace the DFS with DAG dynamic programming. Drop the back edges already found by analyze_loops, iterate blocks in RPO, and compute len[v] = 1 + max(len[p]) in O(B+E). Count paths the same way (cnt[v] = Σcnt[p], saturating or log2/BigUint) instead of relying on #SAT for metrics. Add a 64-sequential-if regression test with a 1 s budget, and a per-function work budget for any remaining enumeration.

title: Kotlin and every non-Java language are parsed by different grammars in different phases; Phase 3 covers this with a raw-token keyword sweep
evidence: Phase 1 parses .kt files with tree_sitter_java (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2 has no Kotlin adapter and falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28,41). Python, Rust, TS, C++ and Go use the JavaScript grammar in both phases (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:29-39,56). Phase 2 then maps JS-grammar nodes onto Java-grammar tokens by (line, col). Phase 3 always uses JavaSemanticAdapter (symbol/mod.rs:38), plus a keyword sweep over raw tokens (pass1_discovery.rs:200-460). Symbols from the sweep have no decl_node, so Phase 4 skips them (cfg/mod.rs:55-58). The sweep turns `var`/`val` locals into SK_FIELDs (pass1_discovery.rs:414-450) and never resets current_class_sym per file (pass1_discovery.rs:257).
impact: Kotlin functions found by the sweep get no CFG, SSA, call edges or activity diagram. Kotlin and Java 10+ local variables appear as class fields. Top-level Kotlin functions attach to a class in another file. The multi-language claims rest on keyword heuristics.
recommendation: Create one LanguageRegistry (grammar, CST reducer, semantic adapter) keyed by LangId and used by Phases 1-3. Add pinned tree-sitter-kotlin and the other grammars, or reject unsupported extensions with a diagnostic. Remove the token sweep once Kotlin reduction exists. Per-language golden fixtures must assert classes, members and per-function CFG counts, plus a test that no SK_FIELD symbol lies inside a method body.

title: Server reads arbitrary files and analyzes arbitrary directories named in requests (no confinement, wildcard CORS, 0.0.0.0)
evidence: The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.rs:32) and sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (306, 327). /api/source tries the raw `file`/`path` query value first (96-121, 200-205): `?file=/etc/passwd` or `?file=C:/Users/u/.ssh/id_rsa` returns the file, and `?file=/dev/zero` makes read_to_string grow until OOM. In /api/analyze, a repo_url ending in `/..` analyzes the server's working directory (393-399), and `a/./../../../../home/u/proj` reaches any directory through parts[2..] (407-414). The URL goes to git clone unvalidated and without `--` (429-437), and a failed clone silently analyzes another user's repository instead (467-482). validate_url (web_repo.rs:97-119) is never called, and it panics itself on `https://github.com/owner`.
impact: Any host on the LAN, or any web page a developer opens (because of the wildcard CORS), can read arbitrary files, exhaust the server's memory, turn arbitrary directories into diagrams, and receive another user's repository results.
recommendation: Serve /api/source only from an allow-listed root, using canonicalize() plus starts_with() as the static route already does (254-272). Accept regular files only (check symlink_metadata) and cap read size (File::take). Bind 127.0.0.1 by default, drop the wildcard CORS and require a token. Parse repo_url with the url crate and accept only https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>. Name each checkout by a hash, pass `--` and `-c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always` to git, and never fall back to another repository.

title: Server turns every panic, abort or hang into a remote outage (single-threaded inline pipeline)
evidence: start() runs handle_connection inline on the main thread (server.rs:40-42). There are no workers and no catch_unwind anywhere in src/. Sockets get a 500 ms read timeout but no write timeout (47). /api/analyze clones the repository and runs all ten phases synchronously, with no time or memory limit (241-253, 366-762). Consequences: a panic (ROB-05), a stack-overflow abort (ROB-08) or a hang (ROB-03) kills or wedges the service; each idle socket stalls it for 500 ms; a client that never reads blocks write_all forever. run.sh:34 serves the dev profile, where the debug_assert at token.rs:122 panics on a 16 MB file of newlines. Dockerfile:49 runs `serve`, which main.rs:544 rejects, so the container exits immediately.
impact: Every robustness defect in the analysis code becomes an unauthenticated one-request kill or hang of the default deployment, and any legitimate large analysis blocks all other users.
recommendation: Run each analysis as a job in a child process, or at minimum on a worker thread with catch_unwind and a 256 MB stack, under wall-clock and RSS limits (setrlimit, or Job Objects on Windows), with a bounded queue that returns 503 when full. Replace the hand-rolled loop with hyper/axum plus tower (TimeoutLayer, RequestBodyLimitLayer, ConcurrencyLimitLayer) and set socket write timeouts. Change the Docker CMD to `server 8080` and smoke-test the image in CI. Done when the ROB-03 and ROB-05 repros return an error and the server keeps serving.

title: Kotlin and 'six-language' support is illusory: Kotlin goes through the Java and JavaScript grammars, everything else through JavaScript
evidence: KotlinLanguageAdapter::ts_language() returns tree_sitter_java::language() (ingestion/adapter/kotlin.rs:29-31). Phase 2's registry has no Kotlin entry, so .kt falls back to the JavaScript grammar (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Kotlin is therefore tokenized as Java and reduced as JavaScript. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ have no adapters and also fall back to JavaScript (ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:34-39). The only grammar dependencies are java and javascript (Cargo.toml:9-11). The CLI ingests only .java/.kt/.kts (main.rs:76-99). Tests and examples contain zero non-Java fixtures, and ROADMAP.md:127 still lists C++/Rust/Go adapters as future work.
impact: Every Kotlin file yields wrong tokens and an AST that disagrees with Phase 1. Python, TypeScript, Rust and C++ input silently produces garbage. The README's F1 = 1.0000 claim is false for five of the six languages it names.
recommendation: Scope the README to Java now and label every other language experimental. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25+/0.26 with a current tree-sitter-java and a real Kotlin grammar (tree-sitter-kotlin-ng). Register one adapter per language for both Phase 1 and Phase 2 from a single table, and return an error instead of falling back to JavaScript for unknown extensions. Add per-language fixture suites in tree-sitter corpus style, and have CI track the rate of ERROR/MISSING nodes per file.

title: Language-neutral, compiler-grade rewiring of your paths (no hard-coding, no templates)
evidence: OpenHeart must support every language with language-agnostic algorithms, and must never hard-code, template or guess: it works the way compilers do, statically. New code is being written now (read what exists): src/lang (neutral.rs universal vocabulary, frontend.rs LanguageFrontend trait, registry.rs single list of languages, profile.rs, build/ for compile_commands, CMake and MSBuild, preprocess.rs, project_model.rs, uml_semantics.rs, idioms.rs, frontends java, kotlin, c, cpp, csharp); src/ir (typed three-address SSA IR with explicit memory operations, lowering from the AST, dominators); src/memory (abstract heap, field-sensitive points-to with on-the-fly call graph, escape, ownership, mod/ref); src/analysis (lattices, worklist solvers, SCCP, intervals, nullness, typestate, control dependence, IFDS/IDE, contexts, canonical branch conditions); src/derive (every diagram derived from those facts with provenance and a Derivation tag, NotDerivable instead of invention); src/symex (bounded static symbolic execution with a stack, heap and path-condition model producing execution traces); src/abi (C/C++ Itanium and MSVC, JVM and CLR memory layouts, lifetimes, calling conventions); src/arch (architecture recovery: dependency graph, DSM, layers, clustering, metrics, boundaries); src/memview (lifetime, ownership, heap-shape and stack-frame views plus memory-safety and data-race facts). Everything from the architectural flow down to memory-level execution must come from these facts, for every language, with semantics exactly per each language specification. Contract names: LangId::C, LangId::Cpp, LangId::CSharp; ASTNodeType additions NN_NAMESPACE_DECL, NN_STRUCT_DECL, NN_UNION_DECL, NN_TYPEDEF_DECL, NN_FUNCTION_DECL, NN_DESTRUCTOR_DECL, NN_OPERATOR_DECL, NN_TEMPLATE_DECL, NN_PROPERTY_DECL, NN_INDEXER_DECL, NN_EVENT_DECL, NN_DELEGATE_DECL, NN_USING_DIRECTIVE, NN_INCLUDE_DIRECTIVE, NN_GOTO_STMT, NN_LABELED_STMT, NN_FOREACH_STMT, NN_USING_STMT, NN_LOCK_STMT, NN_YIELD_STMT.
impact: Without this, OpenHeart stays Java-specific and heuristic instead of a universal, compiler-grade engine.
recommendation: Add pub mod lang; pub mod ir; pub mod memory; pub mod analysis; pub mod derive; pub mod symex; pub mod abi; pub mod arch; pub mod memview; to src/lib.rs plus every mod declaration listed in handoffs; make CLI and server discovery, supported-language lists and API responses come from src/lang/registry.rs and profile.rs; accept C, C++, C#, Java and Kotlin projects including compile_commands.json, CMake and .sln/.csproj inputs; run the new pipeline stages.

title: Position and identifier model is byte- and ASCII-based; one long line aborts Phase 1
evidence: src/ingestion/walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps, in the sort key's 16-bit column (src/core/types/token.rs:121-124). On a line longer than 65,535 bytes, a later token can collide with an earlier, non-adjacent one. The dedup handles only adjacent keys (src/ingestion/mod.rs:140-154), so finalize fails with 'Invariant 2 Violation' (src/ingestion/builder.rs:49-56). The server collects .js files from everywhere except a few directory names (src/adapters/server.rs:764-866), for example a committed javadoc jquery-*.min.js. src/ast/reducer.rs:56 saturates the column instead of wrapping it. Sources are parsed as raw bytes with no BOM or charset handling. Identifier checks need an ASCII first byte (pass1_discovery.rs:687,714,766,803), and class_diagram.rs:98-101 rejects non-ASCII and '$' names.
impact: One minified or generated file aborts the server's analysis of a whole repository. Unicode identifiers (legal in Java, Kotlin, Python, JS, Rust and Swift) and '$' names disappear. Columns are UTF-8 bytes, not the UTF-16 units editors use.
recommendation: Anchor tokens on u32 byte offsets and derive line/col lazily from a line index. If the packed key stays, widen columns to u32 and break ties globally by token_id. Skip and report minified or generated files using linguist-style rules (line length, .min.js, generated-file headers). Transcode non-UTF-8 input (BOM sniffing, encoding_rs), use Unicode XID rules (unicode-ident crate) for identifiers, and expose UTF-16 columns to the web studio and LSP clients.

title: Advertised language support is not backed by code

CHANGELOG.md:32 claims multi-language support 'across all 10 compilation pipeline phases without hardcoded dependencies'. ROADMAP.md:27 ticks multi-language support while :127 leaves the C++/Rust/Go adapters open. docs/codebase-guide.md:86 cites Java/Kotlin/Rust stubs, but only java_stubs.rs exists. src/main.rs:41 says .java while :79-93 also accepts .kt/.kts. The paper (docs/openheart_research_paper.tex:735-741, 1326-1330) claims scope graphs and stubs at language boundaries. The Pages studio's 'AST parsing' (README.md:57) is a regex that requires '{' (web/js/github-engine.js:291) and invents classes from file names (:383-397). docs/overview.md:102-113 lists no Python, TS or C++ repository.

recommendation: Publish a per-language capability matrix generated from conformance tests. Rows are languages; columns are parse, symbols, imports, CFG, SSA, call graph and each diagram. Use tiers: Tier 1 (full pipeline), Tier 2 (outline via tree-sitter tags.scm), unsupported. Serve /api/supported-languages from the registry. Withdraw the F1 claim until an independent benchmark exists, and label the web studio's regex mode in the UI.

title: LabelExtractor slices UTF-8 labels by byte and panics on non-ASCII tokens, aborting Phase 9
evidence: `&label_text[..max_chars.saturating_sub(3)]` slices by byte length. It runs for every non-entry/exit block (max 30). node_attr is misused as a token index, so it reads token 0 or op<<12 (e.g. token #86016 for `==` conditions). A token such as 'Bitte geben Sie Ihr Passwört ein', or CJK text, puts byte 27 in the middle of a character (checked in Python), so the slice panics.
impact: Phase 9 crashes on such input. The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind, so a crafted repo sent to /api/analyze is a remote DoS.
recommendation: Truncate on char boundaries (char_indices().nth(n)) and never byte-slice a String. Add test_extract_label_multibyte_truncation with umlaut and CJK tokens. This differs from UML-12, which is about reading the wrong token.

title: Git credential prompt freezes the whole server
evidence: server.rs:429-437 runs git clone via Command::output() with the inherited environment, no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, no askpass override and no timeout. GitHub answers HTTPS clones of nonexistent or private repos with 401, so git prompts for a username on the controlling TTY (run.sh/run.bat) or Git Credential Manager opens a GUI on Windows. Differs from SRV-04: an indefinite hang, not slowness.
impact: One mistyped repo URL blocks every client until someone answers the console prompt.
recommendation: Spawn git with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, GIT_ASKPASS/SSH_ASKPASS set to a no-op, -c credential.helper=, ssh BatchMode, stdin null, and a wall-clock timeout that kills the child. Test: cloning a nonexistent GitHub repo fails within the timeout.

title: Clones run with the operator's git credentials (confused deputy)
evidence: The clone (server.rs:429-437) inherits the server user's credential helpers, ~/.git-credentials and SSH agent. Any page can POST a private repo URL the developer can access (CORS * at server.rs:327), then read the files from ./target_repos via /api/source (server.rs:211). Differs from SRV-02: even a strictly validated https://github.com/owner/repo URL leaks private code.
impact: Any website can exfiltrate a developer's private repositories while the studio is running.
recommendation: Clone in an isolated credential context: HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to an empty temp dir, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, -c credential.helper=, ssh disabled, anonymous https only; make private-repo access an explicit opt-in token. Test that a private repo URL fails.

title: A panic in any request or phase kills the server process
evidence: start() calls handle_connection on the main thread (server.rs:40-42) with no catch_unwind and no worker thread. Phases 1-9 run inline (server.rs:527-617) and contain asserts and unchecked slicing (src/ast/builder.rs:180, src/ast/mod.rs:58-59). run.sh launches a dev build, where debug_assert! is active (token.rs:122).
impact: One unusual or crafted repository terminates the service for everyone and leaves temp dirs behind.
recommendation: Run each request on a worker thread, or wrap it in catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe. Turn panics into logged 500 responses and keep accepting. Test: a handler that panics returns 500 and the next request succeeds.

title: Server directory walkers follow symlinks (loops, exponential traversal, escapes)
evidence: collect_files (server.rs:777-804) and walkdir_find::visit (server.rs:345-347) recurse on path.is_dir(), which follows symlinks, and git checks symlinks out on Linux and macOS. Links a->. plus b->. give about 2^40 traversals before ELOOP. A link to / walks the host filesystem. One loop link re-collects every file about 40 times. Differs from SRV-01 (direct path read).
impact: One public repo can hang the serial server, duplicate classes, or pull host files outside the clone into the analysis.
recommendation: Use DirEntry::file_type()/symlink_metadata and skip symlinks, or canonicalize and require targets under the repo root. Track visited (dev, inode) pairs and cap depth and file count. Tests: fixture with self-loop links and a link to an outside directory.

title: Symlinked source files are read through to devices and host files
evidence: collect_files keeps any entry with a code extension without checking that it is a regular file (server.rs:805-884), and ingestion follows the link in fs::metadata/fs::read (src/ingestion/mod.rs:51-54). A cloned Evil.java -> /dev/zero grows memory until OOM. X.java -> /etc/... pulls host files into results and, via walkdir_find, into /api/source. The CLI has the same gap (main.rs:90-95).
impact: One public repository can crash the server with OOM or expose host files through analysis output.
recommendation: Accept only regular files using DirEntry::file_type() without following links, or canonicalize and require targets inside the repo. Cap per-file size before reading. Test: a symlink to /dev/zero is skipped.

title: Clone cache keyed only by the URL's last path segment
evidence: repo_url maps to ./target_repos/<last segment> (server.rs:393-399), and an existing directory is reused (server.rs:460-465) without checking owner, remote, branch or commit. alice/utils and bob/utils share one directory. Clones are never refreshed. A clone interrupted by restart_server.sh kill -9 is later treated as complete. Differs from SRV-07 (fallback when the dir is missing).
impact: Users silently receive another owner's code, stale code, or a partial checkout reported as success.
recommendation: Key the cache by normalized host/owner/repo plus resolved commit, and verify git remote get-url origin. Clone into a temp dir and rename atomically on success. Refresh or expire entries. Test: two owners with the same repo name get different analyses.

title: restart_server.sh SIGKILLs every process using the port, including clients
evidence: lsof -t -i:${PORT} (restart_server.sh:11) matches sockets whose local or remote port is 8080. That includes browsers, IDEs and any app connected to a remote :8080 service or proxy, and all of them are killed with kill -9 (line 14) without confirmation. Both make server and make serve run it (Makefile:39-44).
impact: Starting the dev server can force-kill unrelated applications and lose unsaved work.
recommendation: Select listeners only (lsof -t -iTCP:$PORT -sTCP:LISTEN) and check that the process is openheart or cargo. Send SIGTERM and wait before SIGKILL, and ask before killing any other process.

title: Docker builder toolchain is likely too old for the locked dependencies
evidence: Dockerfile:2 pins rust:1.80-slim. Cargo.lock pins sha2 0.11.1 (digest 0.11.3, hybrid-array 0.4.15) and getrandom 0.4.3; these release lines use edition 2024 and need Rust 1.85 or later. Cargo.toml has no rust-version, and CI tests only stable and beta (ci.yml:19). Differs from SRV-11: the image cannot be built at all.
impact: docker build fails while compiling dependencies, even after the CMD in SRV-03 is fixed.
recommendation: Pin a current toolchain image by digest, declare rust-version in Cargo.toml, and add MSRV and docker-build CI jobs.

title: Unbounded recursion on the 1 MB main thread: deep CST, CFG, dominator, BDD or call-graph inputs abort the process
evidence: Recursion depth grows with the input in: ingestion/walker.rs:32-71 and ast/reducer.rs:8-68 (CST depth; long + chains and else-if chains nest one level per term); cfg/stmts/if_stmt.rs:34,49; rpo.rs:7, loops.rs:29, postdom.rs:24 and ssa/cdg.rs:37 (DFS depth ≈ block count); ssa/renaming.rs:103-192 (dominator-tree depth, 12-argument frames); liveness.rs:165; bdd/apply.rs:103-104,137-138 and sat_count.rs:79 (≈ variable count); cg/scc.rs:63-85 (Tarjan). Everything runs on the main thread (main.rs, server.rs:40-41), whose default stack is 1 MB on Windows/MSVC and 8 MB on Linux.
impact: A stack overflow aborts the process rather than panicking. The CLI or the HTTP server dies on one deep generated file (JFlex/ANTLR output, huge initializers) with no partial output, and an attacker can kill the server through /api/analyze.
recommendation: Convert these routines to explicit-stack iteration: TreeCursor goto_first_child/goto_next_sibling/goto_parent loops, (node, child_idx) DFS frames, Pearce's iterative SCC (petgraph::algo::tarjan_scc), and an iterative apply with an ITE cache. As a stopgap, run the pipeline on std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(512<<20). Add stress tests: a 100K-term concatenation, a 20K-branch else-if chain and a 50K-block method.

title: Single-threaded pipeline that reads every file three times and parses it twice
evidence: Cargo.toml has no rayon or any other parallelism crate, and core/pipeline.rs:170-225 and main.rs:150-254 run the phases strictly serially. Phase 1 reads each file twice (ingestion/mod.rs:53, 111) and parses it with a single Parser (108); the Mutex-wrapped interner (105) is never shared across threads. Phase 2 re-reads and re-parses every file (ast/mod.rs:142-143). Kotlin is parsed with the Java grammar (kotlin.rs:30) and then with the JavaScript fallback, because no Kotlin AST adapter is registered (ast/adapter/registry.rs:19-28). Phases 4, 5, 8 and 9 loop over functions serially.
impact: Uses one core and pays twice the front-end parse cost. Kotlin-heavy repos pay wrong-grammar error recovery twice. About 8–12× of the available throughput on 16 cores goes unused.
recommendation: Parse once and emit tokens plus the reduced BP AST in the same walk. Run rayon par_iter over files with a per-thread tree_sitter::Parser (map_init), discover files with the ignore or jwalk crate, and merge per-file interners (or use lasso::ThreadedRodeo). Assign token ids from per-file counts plus a prefix sum. Use par_iter over functions in Phases 4, 5 and 8 and over classes in Phase 9; ruff and Biome use this per-file model.

title: No incremental or persistent reuse: .scpg is a stub, the delta engine is a no-op, and global ids renumber on every edit
evidence: scpg/serializer/mod.rs:56-108 writes 4-byte counts for 10 of 11 sections (e.g. line 59); only StringTable (62) carries data. MemoryMappedSCPG::open (scpg/mmap/mod.rs:18) uses fs::read rather than mmap, and no query can be served from the file. scpg/incremental/mod.rs:28 'applies' a delta by XOR-ing the hash. Token, preorder and symbol ids are corpus-global, so tra/delta/mod.rs:28-39 invalidates every symbol after the first changed token. main.rs keeps nine artifacts plus six raw byte copies alive until exit.
impact: Every run and every server request is a cold full rebuild, and peak RSS is the sum of all phases (several GB at 1M LOC). The 'O(1) incremental delta update' marked done in ROADMAP.md:116 does not exist.
recommendation: Use stable file-local ids such as (file_id, local_idx) or rust-analyzer-style AstIds. Cache per-file Phase 1–5 outputs keyed by BLAKE3(content + config), as ruff's cache does, and express cross-file phases as Salsa queries. Persist real CSR sections with zero-copy views (rkyv, zerocopy or bytemuck over memmap2) so open() can answer queries. Drop each phase's inputs once they are consumed.

title: HTTP server runs analyses synchronously on a single-threaded accept loop with no budgets, queue or cache
evidence: adapters/server.rs binds 0.0.0.0 (32) and handles connections one at a time on the accept thread (40-41). /api/analyze (252) runs git clone (429), all ten phases (506-617) and every exporter inside the request, with no timeout, cancellation, CPU or memory budget, or input-size cap. Output goes to the shared web/diagrams directory (637), so sessions overwrite each other. The response is assembled with format! through a five-pass .replace escaper (701-707). Nothing is cached by repo and commit.
impact: One large or adversarial repository (see SCALE-01 and SCALE-05) blocks or kills the service for everyone, including /api/health. Throughput is one analysis at a time, and every repeat request recomputes everything.
recommendation: Move to axum/hyper on tokio and run jobs on a bounded worker pool (spawn_blocking or rayon). Return 202 with a job id, and stream progress over SSE. Enforce per-job wall-clock and work budgets through cancellation tokens checked inside phase loops. Use per-job output directories, an artifact cache keyed by (repo URL, commit SHA), and streaming serde_json responses.

title: Traceability stops at Phase 9: exporters ignore UMLLink spans and fabricate file names and line numbers
evidence: Phase 7 computes exact (file_id, line, col) UMLLinkRecords, and Phase 9 copies them into ClassRecord.uml_link (class_diagram.rs:304-319). No exporter under src/scpg reads uml_link, uml_link_node or uml_link_token. The JSON IR the studio loads sets file to '<Name>.java' and lines to [1, 5, 10] (json.rs:267-268; also 580-581, 671-672, 733-734) and hard-codes 'OpenHeartEngine.java' (json.rs:1447). The editor requests /api/source by that guessed name (editor.js:160-161). The server then matches it by file stem across fixed example folders (server.rs:109-224). NavigationEngine::to_source and from_source are linear scans (navigation.rs:9-27).
impact: Click-to-source is wrong for Kotlin files, files with several classes, nested classes and duplicate names, and it always highlights lines 1, 5 and 10. The O(1) source-to-diagram traceability claim therefore fails at the UI.
recommendation: Attach a source anchor to every diagram node and edge: root-relative path, start/end line and column, and token range, taken from ClassRecord.uml_link and MessageRecord.uml_link_token. Serve sources by (session, file_id), never by name. Make to_source an O(1) index (uml_links is already sorted by sym_id) and from_source an interval-tree lookup. Done = for each fixture class, the JSON anchor equals the declaration position reported by JavaParser or javac.

title: Four separate pipelines (CLI, server, test builder, browser) give different results for the same repository
evidence: The CLI analyzes .java/.kt/.kts files, tests included (main.rs:76-99). The server takes 58 extensions and drops test and build dirs and *Test files (server.rs:770-884). It never calls Phase10Stage yet reports 'All 10 phases verified' (server.rs:619-699), and it swallows IO errors with unwrap_or_default (server.rs:536-609). It ignores the client's diagram_types (api.js:36 vs server.rs:366-372) and writes into the git-tracked web/diagrams shared by every session (server.rs:636-691). SCPGPipelineBuilder, the only path the tests use, writes graph.scpg instead of unified.scpg and ignores diagram_formats (pipeline.rs:100,143-148,168). The browser engine regex-parses only the first 30 files and uses a random compiler_hash (github-engine.js:102,576). The Dockerfile runs `openheart serve`, which main.rs rejects (main.rs:532,544; Dockerfile:49).
impact: The same repository gives different classes and diagrams depending on entry point. Tests and the F1 harness validate paths the CLI does not run. Concurrent sessions overwrite each other's diagrams, and the Docker image exits at startup.
recommendation: Expose one library entry point, Pipeline::run(&AnalysisConfig) -> Result<AnalysisOutputs, PipelineError>, with include/exclude globs, languages and formats. Call it from the CLI, the server and the tests, and delete the copies. Have the server write per-session directories served under /sessions/{id}/ and never touch web/. Add a contract test asserting byte-identical CLI and server outputs for a fixture, fix the Dockerfile CMD, and regenerate the Pages demo from the engine in CI.

title: Most computed IR is never consumed, and the persisted artifacts cannot be reloaded: .scpg stores counts and .ssa reads back empty
evidence: SCPGSerializer writes a 4- or 8-byte count for 10 of 11 sections and real bytes only for strings (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:56-108). OpenHeartEngine holds a hash and an empty cache (scpg/api/mod.rs:29-45). SSASerializer::read returns no functions (ssa/serializer.rs:167-205). The CDG, def-use CSR, dominators, dominance frontiers, loop info, points_to_table and the TRA bi_ast/bi_blk/bi_ssa/bi_cs/cs_span indexes have no consumer outside their own modules except inspect printing their lengths (main.rs:397,435-439). Phase 9 computes activity labels and discards them (activity_diagram.rs:82-93), and label_texts is never filled (uma/types.rs:282). Artifact files are re-read only to compute CRCs (main.rs:154-226).
impact: Nothing can be queried, resumed or diffed from disk. The 'unified memory-mapped SCPG' and its compression figures describe a file with no data, and most Phase 4-8 work cannot change any output.
recommendation: Make .scpg the real database: store each section as a schema-versioned, zero-copy encoding of its artifact (rkyv, FlatBuffers or Cap'n Proto), memory-mapped, with section CRCs verified on open. OpenHeartEngine::open must answer queries with no in-memory artifacts, as a CodeQL database or Joern's persisted flatgraph CPG does. Add a test that fails when an artifact field has no consumer, plus an e2e test that analyzes, reopens the .scpg and runs a slice and a reachability query.

title: Error handling is inconsistent across phases: global aborts on local faults, silent skips, panics, and invariants met by editing data
evidence: One unreadable file or a None parse aborts Phase 1 (ingestion/mod.rs:51-54,111,117), and one odd function aborts Phases 4 and 5 (cfg/mod.rs:84; ssa/mod.rs:81). Yet Phase 2 silently skips files it cannot read or parse (ast/mod.rs:141-154). Phases 7-10 return no Result and panic or assert instead (tra/mod.rs:42-44; tra/builder.rs:67-130; psa/mod.rs:153-155; uma/mod.rs:97-99; scpg/mod.rs:53-55). The single-threaded server has no catch_unwind (server.rs:40-42). Invariants are met by editing data: empty blocks map to token 0 (blk_bi.rs:17-21), orphans are moved under symbol 0 (pass1_discovery.rs:622-627), and hierarchy cycles are deleted (pass5_hierarchy.rs:218). thiserror is a dependency but is never used, and error JSON interpolates Debug paths (server.rs:530-533).
impact: Large repositories fail completely on one bad unit, or degrade silently. One panic stops the server for every user, and real resolution bugs stay hidden. The CLI prints 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' even when diagram writes fail (main.rs:289-341).
recommendation: Define a StageError enum with thiserror. Make every stage return Result and record per-file Diagnostics (file, phase, kind, message) in a diagnostics table, as CodeQL extractors do, continuing past local faults. Turn invariant checks into reported errors, never data patches. Run each server request under catch_unwind or in a worker pool, and build every response with serde_json. When a run is degraded, exit non-zero and report the skipped files and failed functions.

title: Traceability in the delivered UI is fabricated, and source lookup is overfit to the example corpus
evidence: Every JSON class node gets `file: "{Name}.java"` and `lines: [1, 5, 10]` (json.rs:267-268), although ClassRecord carries a real UMLLink; other views use `lines: vec![1]` (581, 672, 734, 1394, 1472). /api/source first tries hard-coded example-pattern folders and ./target_repos/FractalAndroid (server.rs:119-198). It then returns the first basename match under ./examples before ./target_repos (207-223), so a user's Application.java can resolve to examples/big_project_src/.../Application.java. If that also fails, editor.js:209-213 synthesizes a Java file with invented method bodies (227-500) and highlights lines in it. server.rs:717 falls back to the name `file_{id}.kt`.
impact: The "O(1) bidirectional traceability" claim fails in practice: Kotlin and TS files, inner classes and multi-class files jump to the wrong file or line, sometimes into example code or synthesized source.
recommendation: Emit the real span (file path from tca, line/col start and end from tra.uml_links) on every node and edge. Serve sources only by a manifest-relative path validated against the analysed tree. Remove the example-directory probes and synthesizeSourceFromNode. Done = a property test asserting that, for every node, the cited file and line contain the declared identifier, plus e2e tests on Kotlin and TypeScript fixtures.

title: Hard-coded name deny-lists and suffix rules silently drop real user classes
evidence: class_diagram.rs:161-165 discards any class whose name ends in "Binding" or appears in a 188-entry list (346-538) that mixes keywords with domain names: Entity, Value, Configuration, Root, Table, Scanner, Context, Update, Insert, Error, Logger and others. The PlantUML view also skips user classes named List, Map, Set, Optional or Character (common.rs:59-91; plantuml.rs:292). The server drops any file whose stem ends in "test", such as Contest.java or Latest.java (server.rs:875-881). Pass 1 rejects classes named Map, Set, Array, Function or Promise (pass1_discovery.rs:356-370). The bundled examples/huge_enterprise_src/enterprise/bank/core/Entity.java, implemented by BaseModel, is dropped.
impact: Common domain models (JPA Entity, Table and Value, Android *Binding classes, a game Map class) lose classes and edges without warning, and FIT-02 ensures the benchmark never notices.
recommendation: Filter by origin, not by name. Library stubs already carry first_token_id and decl_node = u32::MAX (java_stubs.rs:127,140), and unresolved types are SK_EXTERNAL. Exclude generated code by configurable path globs, and identify test sources from build metadata (Gradle/Maven sourceSets, Cargo targets) instead of filename suffixes. Done = a fixture with classes named Entity, Table, Map, Contest and FooBinding appears complete in every exporter.

title: A missing or failed repository is silently replaced by another repo and reported as success
evidence: When ./target_repos/<name> is absent and `git clone` fails, process_analyze_request takes the first directory in ./target_repos (server.rs:467-482). It analyses that directory and returns `"status":"success"` with the log "All 10 phases verified" (696-699). The payment-service preset (index.html:93, 1155) points at https://github.com/example/payment-service, which can only succeed through this fallback. Benchmark scripts gate on status and syntax only (verify_all_14_uml_diagrams.py:132-149), so a missing dataset produces green results computed on the wrong code.
impact: A typo, a private repo or an absent dataset returns another project's diagrams under the requested name. Published benchmark numbers can come from the wrong repository without any warning.
recommendation: Fail closed: return an error status (and HTTP 4xx) when the requested repository cannot be materialized. Include the resolved path and commit SHA in every response. Benchmark scripts must assert that the analysed SHA equals the pinned SHA from a dataset manifest. Done = an integration test where an unknown repository yields an error and no diagrams.

title: 16-bit column in sort keys: one line longer than 64 KB aborts the whole repository run
evidence: walker.rs:59 stores `col: start.column as u16`, which wraps. build_sort_key packs file (u16), line (u24) and col (u16) into one key (token.rs:121-124), and the duplicate counter only separates consecutive equal keys (ingestion/mod.rs:140-155). Two tokens on one line at columns c and c+65,536 therefore get the same key, and finalize returns 'Invariant 2 Violation (Injectivity)' (builder.rs:49-55). A port of this logic finds 2,232 duplicate keys in a single 70 KB line. The server also ingests .js files (server.rs:816), so a committed jquery.min.js under src/main/resources/static fails the analysis, and long generated Java/Kotlin lines do the same. reducer.rs:56 clamps the column instead of wrapping it, so Phase 2 lookups disagree with Phase 1.
impact: A single minified or generated file makes the entire run fail with no partial output. A file with more than 16,777,215 lines (line & 0xFFFFFF) has the same effect.
recommendation: Identify tokens by (file_id u32, byte_offset) or by a per-file ordinal, and keep line and column in separate u32 tables, as tree-sitter's Point does. If packing stays, saturate and flag instead of wrapping. Turn the injectivity check into a per-file diagnostic that skips the offending file rather than failing the run. Add boundary tests: a 70 KB line, a 16.8M-line file, and minified JS.

title: Source discovery follows symlinks with no cycle, file-type or root checks, and one bad file aborts the run
evidence: collect_source_files (main.rs:84-96), collect_files (server.rs:764-804) and walkdir_find (server.rs:342-361) recurse whenever Path::is_dir() is true, and is_dir() follows symlinks. None of them keeps a visited set, caps depth or confines paths to the repository root. A cloned repo containing `a -> .` and `b -> .` makes traversal exponential. `Big.java -> /dev/zero` passes the extension filter, and fs::read (ingestion/mod.rs:53) reads until memory runs out. `x -> /` ingests the host filesystem. Per-file failures are fatal: a dangling symlink fails fs::metadata (ingestion/mod.rs:51-52), and the CLI's `?` (main.rs:85-86) turns one ENAMETOOLONG from a self-link into 'Failed to scan directory'.
impact: Malicious repositories, and merely messy ones (dangling links are common), hang the run, exhaust memory or abort the whole analysis. The server can also be steered into reading outside the clone.
recommendation: Use the ignore crate (ripgrep's walker) with follow_links(false), same_file_system(true), max_depth and .gitignore support. Accept only entries where symlink_metadata() reports a regular file and the canonicalized path lies under the repository root. Cap per-file size (configurable, e.g. 8 MiB) with File::take. Record per-file errors as diagnostics and continue, as ruff and rust-analyzer do.

title: Real Rust engine is effectively unreachable; backend results are discarded
evidence: index.html:861-862 aborts the /api/analyze request after 2,500 ms. The server, however, runs a synchronous `git clone --depth 1` plus all ten phases before it replies (src/adapters/server.rs:424-441), so real repos fall back to the regex engine. When the backend does answer in time, the UI ignores its payload (index.html:888-907). It re-fetches `diagrams/<type>.json` (graph-canvas.js:625), which the server has overwritten in the shared web/diagrams folder (server.rs:636-660), and any active customGraphIr takes precedence (graph-canvas.js:604-606). Engine `errors` are swallowed silently (index.html:877-884).
impact: Users rarely see the engine the README benchmarks. Concurrent users overwrite each other's results, committed demo assets get overwritten, and a previous local codebase can be shown under a new repo's name.
recommendation: Turn analysis into an async job API: POST returns a job id, progress arrives via SSE or WebSocket, and the job can be cancelled. Render the returned IR directly from session-scoped artifact URLs, and never write into web/. Show engine errors to the user. Longer term, compile phases 1-9 to WebAssembly (wasm-bindgen plus web-tree-sitter grammars) and run them in a Web Worker, so GitHub Pages runs the same analyzer and the regex engine can be retired.

title: Artifacts are non-deterministic (wall-clock time, file mtimes, raw paths), so the hash chain changes on every run
evidence: The .tca header embeds SystemTime::now() (ingestion/serializer.rs:80-84), each file's mtime_ns (ingestion/mod.rs:62-67, written at serializer.rs:115) and paths exactly as passed in. Phase 2 hashes the whole .tca (ast/mod.rs:48) and each later phase chains on upstream bytes. As a result, identical source yields different hashes in all ten artifacts on every run, and so does a git checkout that only touches mtimes. The .scpg header adds now_ns and writes source_hash as zeros (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:136-146). The published demo diagrams are whatever the last local server run wrote into web/diagrams (server.rs:637).
impact: Staleness and incremental detection (the paper's Eq. 8, 'O(1) invalidation') can never report 'unchanged'. Byte-level golden tests, build caching and cross-machine reproduction of benchmark artifacts are all impossible.
recommendation: Make serialization a pure function of content. Drop wall-clock time and mtimes from hashed bytes; if needed, keep them in an unhashed sidecar that honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Store project-relative paths normalized to '/', and chain on content digests (BLAKE3 or SHA-256 over canonical sections) rather than whole-file CRCs. Generate demo diagrams in CI from a pinned input. Add a CI job that runs the pipeline twice, on two OSes, and byte-compares every artifact, as reproducible-builds.org recommends.

title: No error model: String errors, an unused thiserror, panics in Phases 7-9, silently dropped files and integer truncation
evidence: thiserror is declared (Cargo.toml:13) but never used, and src has no error enum. 27 signatures return Result<_, String>, and callers re-stringify errors with {:?}. Phases 7-9 return bare artifacts and panic! when a write fails (tra/mod.rs:43, psa/mod.rs:154, uma/mod.rs:98). Phase 2 silently skips any file it cannot read or parse (nested `if let Ok`, ast/mod.rs:140-152). The server hashes `fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default()` (server.rs:536-609). `file_id as u16` (ingestion/mod.rs:70) wraps past 65,536 files and `column as u16` (walker.rs:59) past column 65,535, although security-architecture.md:26 claims these values saturate. 291 unwraps remain.
impact: A full disk or a permission error aborts the server. Unreadable files vanish from the results with no warning. Large monorepos and minified files get colliding sort keys and wrong traceability, all silently.
recommendation: Define typed errors per layer with thiserror, for example ArtifactError {Truncated, BadMagic, CrcMismatch{expected, found}, Version} and IngestError {Io{path}, Parse{path}}, and use anyhow or miette only in the CLI. Make every stage return Result, and record per-file diagnostics instead of skipping files. Replace `as` casts with u16::try_from plus explicit errors, or widen the IDs. Deny clippy::unwrap_used, expect_used, panic and indexing_slicing in library code, following the Rust API Guidelines (C-GOOD-ERR).

title: Integrity checks are untested and partly fake: 'VERIFIED VALID' without a CRC, a non-standard PSA CRC, a count-based hash chain
evidence: cmd_inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa after matching only the magic number (main.rs:373-388). psa::crc64_ecma (psa/serializer.rs:259-279) yields 0xD428DA62D41203D6 for '123456789', while the catalogue CRC-64/ECMA-182 value, which ingestion's copy matches, is 0x6C40DF5F0B497347. Its doc claim to match the other serializers is therefore false, and its only test checks determinism (334-340). ScpgHashChain hashes the file count as 'bpa_hash', call_site_count as 'cga_hash', and a Debug string that includes mtime_ns (hash_chain.rs:36-41). The only test asserts scpg_hash != 0. No test flips a byte.
impact: Corrupt .tca and .bpa files are reported as valid, and standard tools cannot verify .psa checksums. Staleness detection misses content edits that keep the counts equal, and fires on a mere touch.
recommendation: Consolidate into one checksum module with known-answer tests against the crc crate's CRC_64_ECMA_182. For every artifact, add a proptest that flips a random bit in the serialized file and asserts read() returns Err, and make inspect call the real readers. Add metamorphic staleness tests: editing a method body while keeping counts equal must change scpg_hash, and touching files or re-checking out without edits must not. Derive the component hashes from artifact bytes.

title: The adapter and registry design forces 25+ file edits per new language
evidence: Two language-id registries disagree: src/ingestion/adapter/registry.rs:19-42 has Kotlin, while src/ast/adapter/registry.rs:16-31 has TS/Rust/Generic. `ext_map` is written but never read (registry.rs:46-48); detect() is a separate hardcoded match (:59-83). File selection differs yet again in src/main.rs:79-93, src/adapters/server.rs:790-881 (which drops '*test' stems such as Latest.java and any /spec package), web/js/github-engine.js:89 and ruthless_config.json. Each file is parsed twice, and Phase 2 re-reads it from disk without checking the stored SHA-256 (src/ast/mod.rs:142). PatternDetectionChain and SCPGPipelineBuilder are used only by tests, and the pipeline is copied by hand (main.rs:150-255, server.rs:526-620). tree-sitter is pinned to 0.20 (Cargo.toml:8).
impact: Adding Python today touches 25+ files across all ten phases: Cargo.toml, both registries, the core type enums, the symbol adapter, stubs and passes 1-5, cfg/stmts, ssa/liveness, cg, uma, four exporters, main.rs, server.rs, the tests, the verifier and the web engine.
recommendation: Make one LanguageFrontend trait and registry the single source of truth. It defines: id; dialects (ts/tsx, kts); extensions plus shebang or linguist-style detection; grammar; token classifier; lowering to the IR; LanguageSemantics; name-binding rules (TSG); and stub data. Parse each file once and hand the tree to Phase 2. Drive the CLI, the server, /api/supported-languages and the verifier from the registry, and run every entry point through SCPGPipelineBuilder. Upgrade to tree-sitter 0.25 (LanguageFn). Done = adding a language means one module plus fixtures.

title: Recursive BDD operations can overflow the stack on large functions
evidence: apply, apply_not, restrict and sat_count recurse once per BDD level, so recursion depth reaches the variable count (the number of CFG edges, up to 65535). The CLI and the server run Phase 8 on the main thread, whose default stack is 1 MB on Windows, and no large-stack worker thread is used. Other walks (count_var_nodes, RPO) already use explicit stacks. [HEAD; the uncommitted rewrite makes apply and not iterative.]
impact: A method with thousands of CFG edges can abort the whole process with an uncatchable stack overflow.
recommendation: Make all four routines iterative with explicit work stacks, or run Phase 8 on a thread with a large configured stack. Test with a 20k-edge straight-line CFG.

title: Phase 7/8 panic instead of returning errors, which kills the HTTP server
evidence: Both stages panic! on write errors. Phase 7 checks its invariants with assert!/assert_eq!, which stay on in release builds, and debug builds panic on canonicity failures. Phase7Stage::run and Phase8Stage::run return plain artifacts, while Phases 3-6 return a Result that the server turns into JSON errors. The server handles requests inline on the main thread with no catch_unwind.
impact: One failing request (full disk, unwritable path, invariant violation) shuts down the server for every user.
recommendation: Return Result from both run() functions, turn the invariant asserts into diagnostics or errors, and wrap request handling in catch_unwind.

title: .cga deserializer pre-allocates from untrusted counts
evidence: deserialize calls Vec::with_capacity(n) for every count read from the file: call sites, CSR arrays, the edge map, points-to and SCCs. CRC-64 is not a MAC, so a crafted file passed to `openheart inspect` with call_site_count = 0xFFFFFFFF asks for about 112 GiB and aborts the process before any read error is returned.
impact: Denial of service against `inspect` or any loader that opens a foreign .cga file.
recommendation: Before allocating, bound each count by the remaining bytes divided by the record size (or grow the vectors incrementally), and reject counts that contradict method_count.

title: A reloaded .tca cannot name its files: read() discards the paths and path_str_offset is reinterpreted
evidence: TokenCorpusArtifact has no path field. read() skips the path section (247-251) and returns the on-disk byte offset in path_str_offset. server.rs:714 and class_diagram.rs:132 resolve that field with interner.lookup_text as a text_id, its in-memory meaning (mod.rs:138), so after read() only file 0 resolves correctly. This differs from CORE-07: it is consumer-side data loss.
impact: Any tool built on TokenCorpusSerializer::read reports wrong file names in traces and in test-file detection.
recommendation: Add a file_paths field filled by both run() and read(), and give path_str_offset one documented meaning. Have write() take paths from the artifact; today a longer file_paths slice panics at serializer.rs:97. Add a round-trip test on resolved paths.

title: Scripts SIGKILL any process listening on the benchmark port
evidence: restart_server.sh:11-14 runs kill -9 on every PID lsof finds on the port. The Python harnesses run 'fuser -k PORT/tcp' (benchmark:155, test_ruthless:276, authored:169, refresh:274, full_suite:253, verify_14:160). Whatever owns 8080 or 8085 (another dev server, a proxy) is killed with no check or prompt, and SIGKILL prevents cleanup.
impact: Running a benchmark can kill unrelated local services.
recommendation: Start the server on an ephemeral port and track its PID. If the port is busy, fail with a clear message. Send SIGTERM and wait before escalating.

title: security-architecture.md has no threat model for the server, git clone or web studio
evidence: The document (1-34) covers only Phase 1 ingestion, hashing and bounds. It never mentions the HTTP server binding all interfaces, /api/source file serving, CORS, cloning user-supplied URLs, request or clone limits, or the studio's GitHub calls. AUTO-01 and AUTO-02 report the code defects; this finding is the missing design document.
impact: Deployers cannot tell what is safe to expose, and reviewers have no stated trust boundaries.
recommendation: Add a threat model covering assets, trust boundaries, default bind address, authentication, request and clone limits, clone sandboxing and a file-access allowlist. Link it from SECURITY.md.

title: Phase10Stage::run panics on I/O failure instead of returning Result
evidence: src/scpg/mod.rs:53-55 wraps SCPGSerializer::write in .expect("Phase 10: Failed to write unified .scpg binary file"). Its callers return Result and use ?/map_err for every other phase: SCPGPipelineBuilder::execute (src/core/pipeline.rs:151, 223) and cmd_analyze (src/main.rs:101, 243). The spec declares -> Result<OpenHeartEngine> (docs/plans/phase10.md:302). The written file is never re-opened to validate it.
impact: A read-only output dir, full disk or locked file aborts the CLI or a library caller instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Return io::Result<OpenHeartEngine> (or a typed error) and propagate it with ? in pipeline.rs and main.rs. Optionally re-open the file with OpenHeartEngine::open to validate it, and pass a PipelineArtifacts-style struct instead of 10 positional parameters.

title: UMASerializer::read trusts every count and offset, so malformed files panic or abort
evidence: After the CRC check, every read is an unchecked slice (bytes[offset..offset+4]). Vec::with_capacity takes the u32 header counts as-is, so a count of 0xFFFFFFFF overflows capacity or aborts on OOM. format_version is read but never validated, offset is never compared with data_end (which is why UML-10's misparse goes unnoticed), and tra_hash is never checked.
impact: `openheart inspect` crashes on an old-version, truncated or crafted .uma with a recomputed CRC, instead of returning an error. This differs from UML-10's layout bugs.
recommendation: Read through a bounds-checked cursor that returns io::Error, reject unknown versions, cap capacities by the remaining bytes, and require offset == data_end. Add a fuzz test fuzz_uma_read.

title: Server collects ~60 extensions the pipeline cannot parse
evidence: collect_files accepts py, rs, go, c/cpp, sh, sql, rb, php, asm and more (server.rs:807-867). AdapterRegistry registers only Java, Kotlin (parsed with the Java grammar) and JavaScript, and sends every other language to a JavaScript-grammar fallback (registry.rs:24-57, kotlin.rs:29-30). The suite's own target, the OpenHeart repo (scripts/test_full_suite.py:129), is mostly Rust, Python and JS.
impact: Shell, SQL, C and Python files are tokenized as JavaScript, which pollutes results and wastes time on polyglot repos.
recommendation: Collect only extensions that have a registered adapter (query AdapterRegistry), make the set configurable, and report skipped-file counts in stats. Test: a repo with Foo.java and build.sh yields only Foo.

title: Directory and test-name heuristics drop production sources
evidence: collect_files skips directories named build, out, dist, vendor, target, test, tests, spec or specs at any depth (server.rs:771-803). It also drops files whose lowercase stem ends in test or tests (server.rs:875-881). Real packages such as com/android/build and org/springframework/test disappear, and classes Contest, Latest and Greatest are dropped, while FooIT and FooSpec tests are kept.
impact: Common Java and Android projects silently lose packages and classes from their diagrams.
recommendation: Exclude build outputs only at module roots (next to build.gradle/pom.xml) and treat only src/test* and src/androidTest* as test roots. Use explicit, case-aware test-name patterns and make filters configurable. Tests: a package named build and a class Contest are kept.

title: CLI and server select different files for the same repository
evidence: main.rs:76-99 includes hidden dirs (.gradle, .idea), build/ and generated sources, test sources and Gradle .kts scripts, and matches extensions case-sensitively. server.rs:764-890 lowercases extensions, skips hidden, build and test dirs and test-named files, and adds ~57 non-JVM extensions.
impact: The CLI and the web studio report different classes, hashes and diagrams for the same input.
recommendation: Move discovery into one library function with an options struct (include/exclude globs, test policy) and use it from both entry points. Test that both select the same files for a fixture tree.

title: CLI scan aborts or double-counts on symlinks and unreadable entries
evidence: collect_source_files recurses via p.is_dir(), which follows symlinks, and propagates every read_dir and entry error with ? (main.rs:84-96). A self-referential link re-collects files until ELOOP, and then the whole analyze fails with 'Failed to scan directory'. A single permission-denied subdirectory also aborts the run.
impact: openheart analyze fails outright, or counts sources twice, on repos with symlinks or unreadable folders.
recommendation: Skip symlinked dirs (or dedupe by canonical path), warn and continue on per-entry errors, and dedupe the final list. Test: a temp tree with a loop link yields each file once.

title: Hand-built JSON responses are invalid for common error strings
evidence: Phase 1-6 error branches insert the raw error string (server.rs:530-604), and ingestion errors contain Debug-quoted paths (src/ingestion/mod.rs:52). The no-sources branch embeds target_dir.display() (server.rs:495-502), which on Windows contains sequences like ./target_repos\FractalAndroid. escape_json_str leaves other control characters unescaped (server.rs:701-707). Node's JSON.parse rejects all three cases.
impact: Clients get a parse error instead of the failure reason; on Windows every missing-sources error is unparseable.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json (json! or Serialize structs), including error paths, and delete escape_json_str. Test: each error branch's body parses with serde_json::from_str.

title: Status codes and error schema do not reflect outcomes
evidence: /api/analyze always answers 200, even for a missing repo_url, malformed JSON or phase failures (server.rs:252-253, 374-382). respond_json labels every non-200 code 'Not Found' (server.rs:321-325). Malformed request lines get no response (server.rs:61-64), and wrong methods get 404 instead of 405. Phase errors also omit the session_id and logs that other errors include.
impact: Clients and monitors cannot detect failures reliably and must parse response bodies.
recommendation: Have handlers return a status plus a typed body: 400 for bad input, 502 for clone failure, 500 for phase errors, 405 with Allow. Use a complete reason-phrase table and one error schema. Add per-route status tests.

title: repo_url is extracted by splitting on quotes, not by parsing JSON
evidence: process_analyze_request takes the fourth quote-delimited token after the first "repo_url" (server.rs:367-370). Emulation shows {"repo_url":null,"branch":"main"} yields 'branch'. A nested {"meta":{"repo_url":...}} key wins over the top-level one. Escaped quotes truncate the value, and \/ escapes are passed to git unchanged.
impact: Valid JSON payloads clone or analyze the wrong repository.
recommendation: Deserialize into a typed AnalyzeRequest {repo_url, branch, diagram_types} with serde_json and return 400 on schema errors. Tests for null, nested and escaped inputs.

title: Session temp directory leaked on every error or panic path
evidence: tmp_path is created at server.rs:506-513 but removed only at server.rs:693. The early returns for Phase 1-6 failures (server.rs:527-605) and any panic skip cleanup, leaving corpus.tca, ast.bpa and other artifacts in the system temp directory.
impact: Every failed analysis leaks disk space indefinitely.
recommendation: Hold the directory in tempfile::TempDir (promote tempfile from a dev-dependency) or a Drop guard so cleanup runs on every path. Test: a forced Phase 1 failure leaves no openheart_sess_* directory.

title: On Windows the temp dir is not deleted while corpus.tca is still mapped
evidence: stage_input owns a MemoryMappedFile of corpus.tca (server.rs:539-546) and lives until process_analyze_request returns, but remove_dir_all runs earlier (server.rs:693). Windows refuses to delete a file with a live mapped view, and let _ = hides the failure.
impact: Under run.bat, even successful analyses leave their artifacts in %TEMP%.
recommendation: Drop stage_input before cleanup (put the pipeline in its own block) and log cleanup errors. Add a Windows CI test that the session dir is gone after a request.

title: Server swallows I/O failures that the CLI treats as fatal
evidence: Artifact reads use fs::read(..).unwrap_or_default() (server.rs:536, 556, 581, 593, 609). The .sta write result is discarded (server.rs:569), and diagram dir and file writes are ignored (server.rs:638, 671-689). main.rs:154-226 propagates the same failures with ?. Stale web/diagrams files also survive a failed export. Differs from SRV-13 (duplicated orchestration).
impact: Empty buffers feed hash links and later phases, and the UI shows a previous repo's diagrams while reporting success.
recommendation: Propagate errors with ? into an error response through a helper shared with the CLI. Delete stale outputs before writing, and list failed exports in errors. Test: an unwritable diagram dir yields an error status.

title: Synchronous /api/analyze runs longer than the studio's 2.5 s fetch abort
evidence: Nothing is written until the clone and the whole pipeline finish (server.rs:241-253, 732-761). The main studio aborts the fetch after 2500 ms (web/index.html:862) and switches to the in-browser engine. The server keeps cloning and analyzing, with no cancellation, job id or progress endpoint. Differs from SRV-04: this is a protocol mismatch, not only throughput.
impact: The main UI never uses the native backend for real repositories, yet each attempt still blocks the server.
recommendation: Make analysis asynchronous: POST returns 202 with a job id, GET /api/jobs/{id} returns status, progress and result, and DELETE cancels. Stop the work when the client disconnects. Test the job lifecycle.

title: /api/source misses trigger full recursive walks of all roots
evidence: When the direct path misses, walkdir_find scans five roots on every request (server.rs:208-223). That includes ./target_repos with every .git objects directory, because hidden dirs are not skipped (server.rs:342-361). It collects all matches instead of stopping at the first, and caches nothing. Differs from SRV-01 (access control).
impact: Every source-view click walks all cached clones, stalling the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Resolve sources from the analysis file table (file_id to repo-relative path) or an index built after each analysis. Skip .git and stop at the first exact match.

title: /api/source returns an arbitrary or wrong file for common names
evidence: walkdir_find returns matches in read_dir order and the first one is served (server.rs:215-217). Duplicate basenames (Main.java, Utils.java across packages or repos) therefore resolve nondeterministically. Matching strips .java/.kt from both names (server.rs:350-354), so Foo.java can resolve to Foo.kt or to an extensionless file named Foo.
impact: The editor shows source from a different class or repository than the node that was clicked.
recommendation: Look files up by repo-relative path from the traceability data. If a basename fallback stays, require exact names, scope it to the active repo, sort candidates, and return 409 with the candidates when ambiguous.

title: /api/source query parsing and percent-decoding are incomplete
evidence: Only %2F, %20 and %2B are decoded (server.rs:96-112). The editor sends encodeURIComponent output (editor.js:160), which also produces %24, %5C, %3A, %26, %25 and UTF-8 sequences, so Outer$Inner.java, Windows backslash paths and non-ASCII names never resolve. Values are cut at a second '=', '+' is not decoded to a space, and lowercase %2f is ignored. Differs from SRV-01.
impact: Source view fails for Windows-produced paths and for many legitimate file names.
recommendation: Decode with a real percent or form decoder (the percent-encoding or form_urlencoded crate) and split pairs with split_once('='). Tests for $, backslash, UTF-8 and '=' inside values.

title: /api/supported-languages advertises languages that are not supported
evidence: server.rs:82-85 lists java, python, typescript, javascript, cpp, rust and go, and omits kotlin. Only Java, Kotlin (via the Java grammar) and JavaScript adapters exist (registry.rs:24-39, kotlin.rs:29-30); every other language falls back to the JavaScript grammar.
impact: Clients are told Python, Rust, Go and C++ work, and get JavaScript-grammar garbage instead.
recommendation: Generate the list from AdapterRegistry with an accuracy or maturity flag per language, and include Kotlin with its caveat.

title: No write timeout: a client that stops reading blocks the server
evidence: handle_connection sets only a read timeout (server.rs:47). write_all for large bodies blocks indefinitely once the peer's receive window fills, both in serve_file (server.rs:310-311) and for analyze and source JSON in respond_json (server.rs:333). Differs from SRV-06, which concerns read timeouts.
impact: One slow or malicious client holding a large response stalls all other requests indefinitely.
recommendation: Call set_write_timeout (for example 10 s), treat a timeout as an aborted connection, and bound the total time per connection.

title: No Host-header validation enables DNS rebinding
evidence: handle_connection never inspects the Host header (server.rs:54-77), so it serves any hostname that resolves to it. A rebinding domain gets same-origin access to /api/analyze and /api/source even after CORS * (SRV-05) is removed.
impact: Restricting CORS alone will not stop malicious websites from reaching the local server.
recommendation: Reject requests whose Host is not in an allowlist (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], configured names) with 421 or 403, and add tests.

title: Credentials embedded in repo_url are logged, echoed and persisted
evidence: The raw URL is printed to stdout (server.rs:384), returned in the response logs (server.rs:387-390, 423-426), and saved by git in ./target_repos/<name>/.git/config. Users commonly paste https://user:token@github.com/... for private repos. Differs from SRV-15 (paths and git stderr).
impact: Personal access tokens leak into terminals, API responses and on-disk clone metadata that /api/source can read.
recommendation: Reject URLs that contain userinfo, or redact it before logging and echoing and strip it from the clone's remote config. Sanitize control characters in logged URLs.

title: GitHub tree/sub-directory URLs are mapped to wrong paths
evidence: For https://github.com/o/r/tree/main/sub/dir, repo_name becomes 'dir' (server.rs:393-398), and the sub-path probe looks for ./target_repos/r/tree/main/sub/dir (server.rs:407-414), which never exists. git is then asked to clone the tree URL, which fails. Non-GitHub URLs split into parts such as 'https:' and an empty string.
impact: Branch or sub-directory URLs, a common way to point at part of a repo, always fail or land on the fallback repo.
recommendation: Parse owner, repo, optional ref and sub-path. Clone owner/repo with --branch <ref> and analyze <clone>/<subpath>. Tests for tree URLs, trailing slash and .git.

title: ./target_repos grows without bound
evidence: Every distinct repo name is cloned into ./target_repos (server.rs:428-437) and never evicted. There is no quota, no per-clone size limit and no cleanup endpoint. Differs from SRV-04 (per-request limits): this is storage that accumulates across requests.
impact: Long-running or exposed servers run out of disk, and basename walks get slower over time.
recommendation: Add an LRU cache with total-size and age limits, per-clone size checks (--filter=blob:limit plus a post-clone size check), and an admin cleanup command.

title: A lone verbosity flag panics the CLI
evidence: main.rs:491 checks args.len() < 2 before flags are stripped. After args.retain (main.rs:499, 505), 'openheart --verbose' or 'openheart --trace' leaves only the program name, and main.rs:508 reads args[1], panicking with index out of bounds. Differs from SRV-10: a crash, not dropped flags.
impact: A trivial invocation crashes with a Rust panic instead of printing usage.
recommendation: Strip flags first, then check how many arguments remain (or adopt clap). Test: running with only --trace prints usage and exits 2.

title: inspect reports 'CRC-64 VERIFIED VALID' without verifying
evidence: For .tca and .bpa, cmd_inspect only compares the magic, then prints the verified line (main.rs:373-389) without calling the readers that check the CRC (ingestion/serializer.rs:175-193, ast/serializer.rs:72-86). It prints the compiled-in TCA_VERSION and a hard-coded '1' instead of the file's version. .scpg section CRC32s are never checked (scpg/mmap/mod.rs:17-79), and deserializer errors are discarded (main.rs:481-484).
impact: Corrupted artifacts are certified as valid, which misleads integrity checks and bug triage.
recommendation: Call TokenCorpusSerializer::read and BPASTSerializer::read, verify .scpg section CRCs, print the file's version, and surface the underlying error. Test with a byte-flipped .tca.

title: Requested diagram types and branch are ignored; web_repo config is dead code
evidence: Clients send diagram_types (web/index.html:869, api.js:34-37), but the server reads only repo_url (server.rs:366-372) and always computes everything. WebRepoConfig {branch, selected_diagrams} and UmlDiagramType (web_repo.rs:8-90) are never used. The module doc promises fetching logic and calls a HashSet-based enum a 'Bitmask' (web_repo.rs:1-8). Differs from SRV-02 (validate_url).
impact: Branches and tags cannot be analyzed, unrequested diagrams waste work, and the public API is misleading.
recommendation: Parse a typed request into WebRepoConfig: pass branch to git --branch, parse diagram names with FromStr for UmlDiagramType, and export only the selected diagrams. Otherwise delete the module, and fix the docs. Test: requesting only class returns only class.

title: Server is hard-wired to CWD-relative paths with no configuration
evidence: The web root 'web' (server.rs:78, 257-258), ./target_repos (server.rs:399, 428), the ./examples roots (server.rs:122-123, 209-210) and the web/diagrams output (server.rs:637) all resolve against the process CWD. OpenHeartServer holds only a port (server.rs:22-29). When started from another directory, every page returns 404 and nothing is logged at startup.
impact: Running the installed binary outside the repo root, or as a service, silently breaks the studio and the clone cache.
recommendation: Add a ServerConfig (bind address, web_root, cache_dir, output_dir, limits) read from CLI or env, validate paths at startup, and default to executable-relative or XDG directories.

title: Dockerfile PORT and HOST environment variables are ignored
evidence: Dockerfile:43-44 sets PORT=8080 and HOST=0.0.0.0, but the port comes only from argv (main.rs:532-537) and the bind host is hard-coded (server.rs:32). Nothing reads either variable. Differs from SRV-14 (.env.example knobs).
impact: On platforms that inject PORT (Cloud Run, Heroku, Render), traffic goes to a port the app never binds.
recommendation: Read PORT and HOST (or OPENHEART_PORT and OPENHEART_BIND) in main, with CLI flags taking precedence, or remove the ENV lines.

title: Bitwise CRC-64 recomputed 19 times over re-read artifacts, whole-file buffers, and duplicate token tables
evidence: ingestion/serializer.rs:16-29 computes CRC-64 bit by bit (8 iterations per byte), and integrity.rs and hash_chain.rs compute CRC-32 the same way. main.rs re-reads .tca, .bpa, .cfa, .ssa and .tra (154, 163, 180, 192, 226) only so later phases can re-hash them: TCA, BPA, STA and CFA are hashed three times each (ast/mod.rs:48; symbol/serializer.rs:42-43; cfg/mod.rs:30-31; ssa/mod.rs:41; cg/mod.rs:45-46; psa/mod.rs:77). Serializers build the whole file in a Vec first, and SymbolTableArtifact::build clones every builder table (symbol/serializer.rs:64-71). TCA stores token_records and token_entries as identical copies (builder.rs:30-31).
impact: At 1M LOC this means gigabytes of bitwise CRC (seconds to tens of seconds) plus redundant I/O, a 2× memory spike per phase, and a TCA of 32 B/token instead of 16.
recommendation: Hash once while streaming through a BufWriter with an incremental hasher, and pass the digest forward in memory. Use a SIMD CRC (crc64fast-nvme or crc-fast), or xxh3 (xxhash-rust) for integrity and BLAKE3 for content addressing. Move builder tables instead of cloning them. Drop the duplicate backward table, since token_id order already equals sort order.

title: The provenance hash chain is inconsistent and partly decorative; each run has two different scpg_hash values
evidence: Phase 7 hashes Debug-formatted file records as tca_hash. It uses crc(file count) as bpa_hash, sta.bpa_hash ^ sta.tca_hash as cfa_hash and crc(call_site_count) as cga_hash (hash_chain.rs:36-41), then re-checks the same XOR (tra/builder.rs:97-109). Phase 10 uses a different XOR whose first input is the token count (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:124-134; integrity.rs:29-38). In it, ssa.cfa_hash and psa.cfa_hash cancel, because both are CRCs of the same .cfa bytes (ssa/mod.rs:41; psa/mod.rs:77). PSA stores the STA hash as ssa_hash (psa/mod.rs:78), and the .scpg source_hash is zeroed (scpg/serializer/mod.rs:146). inspect reports 'VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa without checking either (main.rs:373-388).
impact: UMLLinks carry a different hash from the .scpg header, so StaleDetector (invalidation.rs:10-12) would flag everything. CFG changes cannot alter the composite hash, and stale or mixed artifacts go undetected.
recommendation: Define provenance once. Every artifact header stores a BLAKE3 or SHA-256 digest of its canonical payload, the digests of its declared inputs and the engine version, like Bazel action keys, Nix derivations or SLSA/in-toto provenance. Loaders verify the input digests. Compute scpg_hash as a Merkle root over sorted (artifact, digest) pairs, never by XOR, and make inspect verify every checksum it reports.

title: Artifact readers trust header counts and offsets, and inspect reports integrity it never checks
evidence: The readers check a CRC-64, which any attacker can recompute. After that they index `buf[offset..offset+4]` without checking how many bytes remain: TRA (tra/serializer.rs:174-280), PSA (psa/serializer.rs:201-245, including `pos = metrics_offset` taken from the file), UMA (uma/serializer.rs:272 onward) and BPA (ast/serializer.rs:118-171). Short files therefore panic. Counts from u32 headers go straight into Vec::with_capacity (symbol/serializer.rs:240, cg/serializer.rs:158, ingestion/serializer.rs:254,296), so large counts abort on a multi-GiB allocation. scpg/mmap/mod.rs:52-62 reads section_count entries unchecked, and get_section computes `start + byte_length` (86-90), which can wrap. inspect prints 'CRC-64 Check : VERIFIED VALID' for .tca and .bpa files without checking anything (main.rs:373-389).
impact: `openheart inspect`, the documented validation tool, panics or aborts on small crafted files and claims integrity it never verified. Library users who load artifacts inherit the same crashes.
recommendation: Parse through one bounds-checked cursor: a Reader that returns Err on short reads, or zerocopy, binrw or scroll. Check `count <= remaining / record_size` before allocating, and use try_reserve and checked_add for offsets. Make inspect verify the CRC for every artifact type and report the real error. Add cargo-fuzz targets for each format, seeded with real artifacts. Done when 24 hours of libFuzzer finds no crash.

title: No work or memory budgets, and several phases scale super-linearly on realistic large inputs
evidence: Nothing bounds per-function or per-run work. Switch constraints perform k(k-1)/2 BDD applies (constraints.rs:122-127), each of which clears the apply cache (bdd/mod.rs:78). edge_index_of is a linear scan on every lookup (rpo.rs:106-108).
