The CFG CSR build is O(blocks x edges) (cfg/builder/mod.rs:150-172). close_node walks every ancestor (ast/builder.rs:163-175). CHA rescans every symbol per call site (cg/resolution.rs:84). The RMQ stores n(log n+1) u32 values (rmq.rs:28-48), about 0.9 GB for 10M BP bits. Each source is read three times and parsed twice, with no size cap or tree-sitter timeout (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; tree_sitter.rs:17-24). OPENHEART_MAX_MEMORY_MB in .env.example is never read.
impact: Giant switches in JavaCC- or ANTLR-generated code, deep nesting and 1M-LOC repositories make phases quadratic or memory-bound. That is a DoS on the server and contradicts the 128x compression claim.
recommendation: Index edges with a HashMap<(u32,u32),usize> or CSR offsets, and build the CSR by counting sort. Encode exactly-one constraints with a linear sequential counter, and keep a persistent computed table with a per-function node budget (CUDD style). Precompute subtype closures for CHA. Replace the sparse table with a range min-max tree (Navarro-Sadakane) or a block-decomposed RMQ using O(n) bits. Parse each file once, and implement the documented memory limits plus Parser::set_timeout_micros.

title: Ten-phase orchestration is hand-wired at 18 call sites through positional raw-hash parameters, and has already broken the hash chain
evidence: The ten-phase wiring is hand-copied at 18 IngestionStage::run call sites: main.rs:150-255, core/pipeline.rs:170-225, adapters/server.rs:527-615 and 13 test files. PipelineStageTemplate (pipeline.rs:34-78) has no implementors. SCPGPipelineBuilder never reads its diagram_formats field and defaults to the shared temp directory with fixed file names (pipeline.rs:113,159-168). Stages take long positional argument lists with adjacent raw `&[u8]` hash inputs (cg/mod.rs:37-38; Phase 9 takes 10 arguments). That plumbing has already broken the chain: psa/mod.rs:78 stores `cfa.sta_hash` in the PSA's 'CRC-64 of the SSA artifact' field (psa/serializer.rs:37).
impact: Every fix must be repeated at 18 sites, and the copies drift: the server ignores errors the CLI reports. Swapped hashes compile without complaint, and concurrent runs with default settings overwrite each other's artifacts.
recommendation: Make one orchestrator the only entry point for the CLI, the server and tests: a typed stage DAG in which each artifact is a newtype carrying its own content digest (for example Artifact<Tca> with .digest()), so hashes cannot be swapped. Default to a per-run tempfile::TempDir. For incremental runs, use Salsa queries (as rust-analyzer and Astral's ty do) instead of re-running every phase. Provide a test helper such as analyze_fixture(src) returning PipelineArtifacts.

title: The single-threaded pipeline reads every file three times, parses each twice, and logs through a logger that formats and flushes on every event
evidence: There is no rayon or threading anywhere, though .env.example:14 advertises OPENHEART_NUM_THREADS, which the code never reads. Each file is read three times (ingestion/mod.rs:53,111; ast/mod.rs:142) and parsed twice (ingestion/mod.rs:117; ast/mod.rs:143). The SHA-256 recorded on the first read is never checked against the later reads. Log call sites run format! before the level check. Every event, whatever its level, is written to two files and flushed under a global Mutex (logger.rs:124-159). Phase 8 logs one INFO line per function (psa/mod.rs:132), and a debug println! remains in library code (generic.rs:27). The external-type lookup scans every symbol for each reference (pass3_types.rs:108-116).
impact: Throughput is single-core and I/O-bound, and the symbol fallback costs O(types x symbols), so large repositories will be slow or appear to hang. A file edited during a run gets tokens that no longer match its recorded SHA.
recommendation: Read each file once into an Arc<[u8]>, parse it once, and hand the tree or reduced CST to Phase 2. Parallelize per file in Phases 1-2 and per function in Phases 4, 5 and 8 with rayon, merging results deterministically. Replace the logger with tracing and tracing-subscriber: EnvFilter on RUST_LOG, per-phase spans, and a buffered non-blocking file writer from tracing-appender. Index external symbols in a HashMap, and confirm the gains with the ENG-08 harness.

title: Distribution is broken: the release workflow has never run and ships an .rlib; the Docker image can neither build nor start
evidence: `git tag -l` is empty, so the tag-triggered release.yml has never run. It sets no `permissions: contents: write` and would likely get a 403 under the read-only default token. It uploads target/release/libopenheart.rlib (release.yml:26), which only the exact rustc version that built it can use. Dockerfile:2 builds with rust:1.80, but the locked sha2 0.11 needs Rust 1.85 ([manifest](https://docs.rs/crate/sha2/0.11.0/source/Cargo.toml)). Dockerfile:49 runs `openheart serve --port 8080`, but the CLI only knows `server [PORT]` (main.rs:532). Versions disagree: 0.1.0 in Cargo.toml and the CLI banner (main.rs:32), 2.0.0 in CHANGELOG.md:10, and SECURITY.md:9-13 lists 1.1.x, 1.0.x and 0.1.x as supported.
impact: Users and anyone reproducing benchmarks have no usable binaries or containers. Version numbers cannot be mapped to code, so bug reports and published results have no anchor.
recommendation: Use cargo-dist (or taiki-e/upload-rust-binary-action) to build Linux, macOS and Windows binaries with SHA-256 checksums, attest them with actions/attest-build-provenance, and attach a CycloneDX SBOM; publish the crate to crates.io. Drive versions and the CHANGELOG with release-plz from conventional commits so tags, Cargo.toml and the CHANGELOG agree. Fix the Dockerfile: rust:1.85+, an exec-form CMD running `openheart server 8080`, a non-root USER and a healthcheck. Build the image in CI.

title: Docs and repo hygiene: a committed LLM prompt, an empty Phase 4 spec, stale paths, and false security and config statements
evidence: docs/RESEARCH_PAPER_NEXT_PROMPT.txt is an LLM instruction ('MAKE SURE THE PAPER IS UNDENIABLY UNCHALLENGED AND CAN'T BE PROVEN FALSE'), yet docs/README.md:29 lists it as 'Prompt specification'. docs/plans/phase4.md is 0 bytes. contributing.md:18 and security-architecture.md:12 cite src/phase1/, which does not exist. security-architecture.md claims #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (:11), value saturation (:26) and configuration via environment variables (:34). .env.example lists five variables, but the code reads only OPENHEART_LOG. examples/README.md:12,34 point to examples/sample_project, which does not exist and is gitignored. web/docs/ duplicates the HTML in docs/, and one copy has already diverged.
impact: Newcomers follow broken instructions, and security reviewers are misled about unsafe code and input handling. The committed prompt invites the reading that the paper was written to be unchallengeable rather than measured.
recommendation: Delete the prompt file, and fill in or remove phase4.md. Build the docs from one source (mdBook or Docusaurus deployed through Pages) and link-check them in CI with lychee. Tie every security and configuration statement to code, or delete it. Make .env.example list only variables the code reads, ideally via clap's env feature. Pull the README into rustdoc with #![doc = include_str!("../README.md")]. Record the major decisions (custom server, custom logger, file hand-off between phases, String errors) as MADR ADRs.

title: Monolithic connection handler with no Request/Response abstraction
evidence: handle_connection (server.rs:46-290) mixes socket I/O, request parsing, an if/else route chain, query parsing and business logic. Handlers write straight to TcpStream, and process_analyze_request returns preformatted JSON strings.
impact: Routes cannot be unit-tested without sockets, and every fix touches one 250-line function.
recommendation: Introduce Request and Response types and a route table whose handlers are pure functions, or adopt a small HTTP crate (tiny_http, axum). Add per-route unit tests.

title: SCPG query engine and XMI exporter are unreachable from CLI and API
evidence: OpenHeartEngine exposes is_reachable, backward_slice and export_xmi (scpg/api/mod.rs:51-83). main.rs uses the engine only for scpg_hash (main.rs:243-337) and has no query subcommand. The server never builds the engine and has no query routes. Neither entry point exports XMI (main.rs:281-309, server.rs:663-691).
impact: The advertised query engine and XMI output cannot be used without writing Rust code.
recommendation: Add 'openheart query <scpg> reachable|slice ...' and a --format xmi option, plus /api/query/* endpoints backed by one engine per session. Test each command.

title: Exporters emit monolithic, unpartitioned diagrams and recompute shared indexes 57 times
evidence: PlantUMLExporter::export_class_diagram (plantuml.rs:274) and JSONExporter (json.rs:121) put every class and edge into one document. main.rs:281-309 runs 19 diagram types × 3 formats serially, and each call recomputes the package maps (json.rs:132-146; mermaid.rs:602-650). Behavioral views take arbitrary samples (.take(6) at plantuml.rs:925,958 and mermaid.rs:1102). JSON is written with to_string_pretty (factory.rs:208). Mermaid's default maxTextSize of 50,000 characters and PlantUML's 4096-px image limit reject diagrams with thousands of classes.
impact: At around 15K classes the class, package and component outputs are tens of MB and cannot be rendered, and the behavioral samples are not representative.
recommendation: Partition output by package or module: one package-dependency overview plus a drill-down diagram per package. Aggregate edges, building on plantuml_optimizer's bundling, and enforce node and edge caps with summary nodes. Compute the class, package and name indexes once per run, export the formats in parallel with rayon, and emit compact JSON.

title: Everything is public, mostly undocumented, stringly typed and in one crate; the CLI and JSON handling are hand-rolled
evidence: lib.rs makes all 12 modules public, including the HTTP server and a module named `core` that shadows Rust's core crate. There are about 970 pub items and 593 pub fields against 3 pub(crate) uses; roughly 27% of pub items have rustdoc, and there are no crate docs and no #![warn(missing_docs)]. Diagram kinds are strings such as 'statemachine', returning Option (factory.rs:314). The CLI strips flags after its length check, so `openheart --debug` indexes args[1] out of bounds and panics (main.rs:491-508), and an invalid port silently becomes 8080 (:534). The server parses JSON with split('"') (server.rs:367-371) and builds responses with unescaped format! strings, even though serde_json is a dependency.
impact: Every internal refactor is a breaking change and semver cannot be checked. The library cannot target wasm32 (a ROADMAP goal) or be embedded without the server, and CLI and JSON edge cases crash or produce invalid output.
recommendation: Split into a workspace: openheart-core (pure, no I/O), openheart-lang-* crates behind features, openheart-cli (clap derive) and openheart-server (serde for all JSON). Expose a small facade, such as Analysis::from_paths(..).run() returning Result<Scpg>, and make internals pub(crate). Model diagram kinds and formats as enums marked #[non_exhaustive]. Follow the Rust API Guidelines, enable #![warn(missing_docs)], and run cargo-semver-checks in CI once the API settles.

title: STA deserialization allocates memory from untrusted counts and lengths
evidence: Header counts go straight into Vec::with_capacity, and each string length goes into read_exact_bytes, which allocates vec![0; len] before reading. CRC-64 is not a MAC, so a 72-byte file with symbol_count 0xFFFFFFFF and a recomputed checksum requests about 256 GiB. The CLI artifact inspector reaches this code.
impact: A crafted or corrupt .sta aborts the process instead of returning an error.
recommendation: Before allocating, check that count × record size fits in the remaining bytes, cap string lengths by the remaining bytes, and use try_reserve. Fuzz SymbolTableArtifact::deserialize.

title: The library pipeline writes graph.scpg where the CLI writes unified.scpg, and exposes no filter or override settings
evidence: SCPGPipelineBuilder names its Phase 10 output graph.scpg, while cmd_analyze and the usage text use unified.scpg. execute() always calls SourceManifest::new, so TokenFilter and language_overrides cannot be set through the builder. This is a concrete divergence on top of CORE-14's copy-paste finding.
impact: Tools that look for unified.scpg miss library output, and comment or doc-comment policy cannot be configured.
recommendation: Define the artifact file names once as shared constants, and add with_filter and with_language_override to the builder (or let it accept a SourceManifest).

title: The Python harness cannot run on Windows, the maintainer's platform
evidence: The scripts depend on fuser and lsof, call 'python3' (full_suite:241) and write under /tmp. The box-drawing and emoji output crashes when stdout is piped on cp1252: in scratchpad, ruthless_verify.py raised UnicodeEncodeError at line 402. full_suite:159-228 runs cargo test while openheart.exe is running, and Windows locks the file against relinking (medium confidence).
impact: Validation results cannot be reproduced on the development machine.
recommendation: Use sys.executable and tempfile, and track PIDs instead of calling fuser. Call sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8'). Stop the server before running cargo test.

title: restart_server.sh and generate_diagrams.py have small robustness bugs
evidence: restart_server.sh uses 'set -e' without pipefail or nounset (2), never validates or quotes PORT (4, 11, 21), and reports 'No existing server' when lsof is missing (11). generate_diagrams.py:25 derives repo_name with replace('.git',''), so 'user.github.io' becomes 'userhub.io', and it accepts '..' as a name, which writes outside output_diagrams/.
impact: Edge cases produce wrong output directories and misleading messages.
recommendation: Use set -euo pipefail, check that the port is numeric and that lsof exists. Strip only a trailing .git and sanitize the directory name.

title: Docs claim CRC-64 on all ten artifacts, but .scpg uses CRC-32 and inspect skips verification
evidence: README.md:59 says all 10 phases produce CRC-64 verified artifacts, and 10_phase_pipeline_overview.md:85 says Phase 10 verifies CRC-64. The .scpg writer uses per-section CRC-32 (serializer/mod.rs:22, 111). 'inspect' on a .scpg prints 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' without checking any checksum (main.rs:469-474). The help text (main.rs:56) lists 6 inspectable types, although inspect handles 10.
impact: Integrity guarantees are overstated, and the inspect output is misleading.
recommendation: Verify the section CRCs in inspect, print a factual status, and correct the docs and help text.

title: Predictable temp path; pre-existing dirs accepted; create errors ignored
evidence: tmp_path is temp_dir()/openheart_sess_<unix nanos> (server.rs:506-512). let _ = fs::create_dir_all (server.rs:513) accepts an existing directory or symlink and ignores failures. On shared hosts, artifacts can therefore be written into a location an attacker created in advance; otherwise later phases fail with confusing errors.
impact: Other local users can tamper with intermediate artifacts on multi-user machines.
recommendation: Create the session dir with tempfile::Builder (random name, exclusive create, mode 0700) and propagate errors.

title: Non-UTF-8 sources are reported missing and may be substituted
evidence: Candidates are read with fs::read_to_string (server.rs:201, 217). A Latin-1 or Windows-1252 Java file fails with InvalidData, and the loop moves on to other candidates or the basename walk. It may serve a different file with the same name, or return 404 'not found on server disk'.
impact: Projects in legacy encodings cannot show source, or show the wrong file.
recommendation: Read bytes and decode lossily (or detect the encoding), and tell 'unreadable' apart from 'not found' in the response.

title: Whole-file reads with no size cap in /api/source and static serving
evidence: /api/source loads any matched file into a String and JSON-encodes it (server.rs:201, 217, 227-232). serve_file reads whole files with fs::read (server.rs:303), with no streaming and no Range support.
impact: Large files (logs, bundles, binaries in clones) cause memory spikes and multi-megabyte responses.
recommendation: Enforce a maximum source size and return 413 above it, stream static files with io::copy, and support Range requests.

title: Hard-coded demo paths baked into /api/source
evidence: direct_candidates hard-codes ./target_repos/FractalAndroid/ and nine design-pattern package directories under two roots (server.rs:119-198), plus fixed search roots including ./web (server.rs:208-214). All 24 strings are formatted on every request. Differs from SRV-01: maintainability, not access control.
impact: Behavior depends on one developer's local layout, and unrelated repositories are probed.
recommendation: Remove the hard-coded candidates and resolve paths relative to the analyzed repo root recorded for each session.

title: Version, health and capability endpoints are hard-coded
evidence: /api/health always returns online, 'OpenHeart SCPG v0.1.0' and plantuml:true (server.rs:80), although the server renders nothing. /api/version hard-codes 0.1.0, build 'production' and release_date 2026-08-22 (server.rs:93), and main.rs:32 repeats v0.1.0. /api/patterns and /api/supported-diagrams are hand-copied lists (server.rs:86-91). The module doc advertises Telemetry, which does not exist (server.rs:2).
impact: Reported versions drift from Cargo.toml, debug builds claim to be production, and health never reflects failures.
recommendation: Use env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), cfg!(debug_assertions) and a build-time git SHA, and derive the lists from the engine. Make the health check test git availability and writable dirs.

title: HTTP/1.1 framing gaps: no Connection: close, abrupt close, absolute-form
evidence: Responses are HTTP/1.1 with Content-Length but no 'Connection: close' (server.rs:305-307, 326-328), yet the socket is closed after one request. Unread request bytes are dropped without shutdown or drain, so the kernel may send RST and destroy the response. Absolute-form targets (GET http://host/path) fall through to 404 (server.rs:254).
impact: Keep-alive clients and large POSTs see sporadic connection resets, and proxy-style requests fail.
recommendation: Send Connection: close (or implement keep-alive), shut down the write half and drain input briefly before closing, and accept absolute-form targets.

title: Every CLI command creates log files in the current directory
evidence: main.rs:488 calls init_logger_from_env, which opens ./openheart_persistent.log (append) and ./openheart_session.log (logger.rs:110-112), even for help, inspect and server. analyze then re-initializes into OUTPUT_DIR (main.rs:129), leaving stray files in the CWD. The server appends all pipeline logs to the CWD files for its whole lifetime, with no rotation.
impact: Repos fill up with log files, read-only CWDs fail silently, and server log files grow without limit.
recommendation: Enable file logging only for analyze and server, with an explicit --log-dir and size-based rotation. Keep help and inspect console-only.

title: Combined or misplaced flags become positional arguments
evidence: When both --trace and --debug or -v are given, the else-if at main.rs:497-506 strips only --trace. 'openheart analyze src --trace --debug' therefore uses '--debug' as OUTPUT_DIR and creates a directory with that name. 'openheart analyze --help' treats '--help' as the source path.
impact: Output lands in surprising locations and errors are confusing.
recommendation: Strip every recognized flag independently and keep the highest verbosity. Support -h/--help per subcommand and reject unknown dash-prefixed arguments.

title: Command output goes through the logger and can be silenced
evidence: inspect results and the analyze summary are printed with log_info (main.rs:311-342, 354-475). OPENHEART_LOG=warn or off (logger.rs:98-107) suppresses them, so openheart inspect prints nothing and exits 0.
impact: Users and scripts lose the command's main output when they lower log verbosity.
recommendation: Print results to stdout directly (optionally as --json) and keep the logger for diagnostics.

title: analyze reports success when diagram export fails and keeps stale files
evidence: main.rs:258 and 289-307 discard create_dir_all and fs::write errors with .ok() and ignore export_diagram returning None. main.rs:311-341 then logs 'SUCCESS' and 'SYSTEM PRODUCTION READY' unconditionally. Diagram files from earlier runs in the same OUTPUT_DIR remain and look current.
impact: Users and CI do not notice missing or stale diagrams.
recommendation: Collect export failures, warn per file, and remove stale outputs first. Exit non-zero, or print a partial-success summary.

title: Artifact bytes depend on how the source path was spelled
evidence: cmd_analyze passes paths exactly as given or joined (main.rs:104-111, 151), and ingestion interns them into the .tca (ingestion/mod.rs:137-138). 'analyze ./src', 'analyze src' and an absolute path therefore produce different .tca bytes, CRC hash links and SCPG hashes. Absolute paths also embed the user's home directory.
impact: Hashes are not reproducible across machines or invocations, and local paths leak into shared artifacts.
recommendation: Store paths relative to the source root with forward slashes and record the root separately. Test that ./src and src give the same SCPG hash.

title: CLI usage text misdescribes inputs, outputs and checks
evidence: print_usage says analyze scans '.java source files' (main.rs:41), but .kt and .kts are included (main.rs:80). It promises 14 UML diagrams as *.puml and *.mmd, but 19 types and .json files are written (main.rs:53, 260-308). inspect lists six artifact types and CRC-64, though .tra/.psa/.uma/.scpg are handled and .scpg uses CRC32 (main.rs:55-56). server claims PlantUML rendering, which does not exist (main.rs:59).
impact: Users get wrong expectations about what the tool accepts and produces.
recommendation: Generate help from the real argument definitions (clap) and correct each description.

title: Usage errors exit 0 or print to stdout
evidence: Running with no arguments prints usage and exits 0 (main.rs:491-494). 'Error:' messages for missing arguments and unknown subcommands use println! (main.rs:512, 526, 545), while fatal errors use eprintln! (main.rs:552).
impact: Scripts cannot detect misuse, and error text ends up in captured stdout.
recommendation: Print errors to stderr and exit with status 2 for usage errors.

title: Startup banner prints an unusable or wrong address; IPv4-only bind
evidence: start() prints the requested address (server.rs:32-38), so port 0 is announced as ':0' instead of listener.local_addr(). The printed http://0.0.0.0:PORT (also restart_server.sh:20) is blocked by current Chrome and cannot be reached on Windows. Only 0.0.0.0 is bound, so clients that resolve localhost to ::1 first fail or retry.
impact: Startup output is confusing, and connections are slow or fail on IPv6-first hosts.
recommendation: Print local_addr() and a browsable http://localhost URL, and support a configurable bind address including [::].

title: Accept errors are silently discarded and can spin the CPU
evidence: listener.incoming().flatten() (server.rs:40) drops accept errors with no logging or backoff. A persistent error such as EMFILE makes the loop spin at full CPU.
impact: Failures stay hidden, and the CPU is burned when file descriptors run out.
recommendation: Match each Result, log errors, and back off on resource-exhaustion errors.

title: Header and body sent in separate writes with Nagle enabled
evidence: serve_file writes the header and the body in two write_all calls (server.rs:310-311) on a socket without set_nodelay. A small body can wait for the client's delayed ACK of the header segment, which takes up to 40 ms on Linux and 200 ms on Windows.
impact: Each static asset may gain latency, which adds up on the single-threaded server.
recommendation: Write header and body from one buffer (or one BufWriter flush) and/or call set_nodelay(true).

title: Static file serving gaps (MIME, charset, decoding, directory index)
evidence: Only js, css, svg and html get a content type (server.rs:274-284), so .png, .ico, .json, .puml, .mmd and .mjs are served as application/octet-stream. '; charset=utf-8' is appended even to binary types (server.rs:306). Extension checks are case-sensitive, request paths are not percent-decoded (server.rs:256), and directories do not resolve to index.html.
impact: MIME types are wrong (module scripts with .mjs fail), and files with spaces or Unicode names cannot be served.
recommendation: Use a complete MIME map and add charset only for text types. Percent-decode the path and then re-validate it, and serve index.html for directories.

title: PlantUML diagrams generated twice; alias types written redundantly
evidence: The 14 PlantUML diagrams are built with PlantUMLExporter::export_* (server.rs:620-634) and again by diag_engine.export_diagram in the 21-type loop (server.rs:640-672). That loop also includes the aliases use_case and state, which write duplicate JSON files. The comment says 19 diagram formats (server.rs:636), and escaping allocates five strings per diagram (server.rs:701-707).
impact: CPU and memory are wasted on large repositories, and the comment is misleading.
recommendation: Generate each diagram once into a map and reuse it for both the files and the response. Handle aliases in routing instead of writing duplicate files.

title: Traceability payload is truncated and mislabeled
evidence: Only the first 10 uml_links are returned, with no total (server.rs:710). 'tid' carries link.sym_id (server.rs:724-725), but the viewer labels the column TOKEN ID (viewer.js:114, 123). A missing file record gets an invented file_<id>.kt name (server.rs:717). Symbol name and sym_kind are left out, and the same list is shown for every projection.
impact: Users see an incomplete and mislabeled traceability matrix.
recommendation: Return paginated links with a total and rename the field to sym_id. Add the symbol name, kind and repo-relative path, and filter per diagram type.

title: Session id is a seconds timestamp; no real SCPG hash is returned
evidence: session_id is sess_<unix seconds> (server.rs:376-380, 733-737), so it collides within the same second and is not tied to any stored session. The server neither runs Phase 10 nor returns any hash, so the studio shows the timestamp's last 8 digits as 'SCPG 0x... Verified' (web/index.html:890-891). This adds to SRV-13's missing Phase 10.
impact: The UI's 'verified hash' badge is made from a clock value.
recommendation: Use random unique ids, and return the real scpg_hash (or the TRA composite hash) as an explicit field.

title: validate_url silently rewrites names and accepts plaintext http
evidence: validate_url accepts http://github.com (web_repo.rs:99) and deletes '..' and backslashes instead of rejecting them (web_repo.rs:111-112), so 'o..x/repo' validates as owner 'ox'. Any characters (?, #, %, spaces) pass, a '.git/' suffix is kept, and the host match is case-sensitive. Tests cover only the happy path (web_repo.rs:126-133). Differs from SRV-08 (index panic).
impact: Once wired in, it could clone a different repository than requested, over a transport open to man-in-the-middle attacks.
recommendation: Parse with a URL parser, require https and host github.com (case-insensitive), validate owner and repo against [A-Za-z0-9._-], and reject rather than rewrite. Add a test for each case.

title: No file-count or file-size caps although file ids are 16-bit
evidence: The server passes every collected file to ingestion (server.rs:484-515) with no count or size limit. Ingestion casts file_id to u16 (ingestion/mod.rs:70, 123), and Phase 2 reads file_count as u16 (ast/mod.rs:59). Repositories with more than 65,535 matching files therefore wrap ids silently. Differs from SRV-04: the results are corrupted, not just slow.
impact: Large monorepos give corrupted cross-file results instead of a clear error.
recommendation: Reject or shard inputs above 65,535 files or above a per-file size limit with an explicit error, and make the limits configurable.

title: Expect: 100-continue is not supported
evidence: The server never sends 'HTTP/1.1 100 Continue' (server.rs:241-250). curl (for bodies over 1 KiB) and .NET clients wait up to a second for it before sending the body. The server's second read times out after 500 ms and answers that repo_url is missing.
impact: Larger analyze payloads from standard clients fail for no real reason.
recommendation: Detect Expect: 100-continue and reply 100 before reading the body, or adopt an HTTP library.

title: Redundant and unreachable checks in collect_files
evidence: target, node_modules and build are tested twice (server.rs:771-773 and 779-781). lower_name == '.git' (server.rs:786) can never match, because names starting with a dot are already skipped (server.rs:770). The '_test', '_tests' and == 'test' checks (server.rs:877-881) are already covered by ends_with('test') and ends_with('tests').
impact: Dead conditions hide the actual filtering rules.
recommendation: Replace them with one declarative exclusion set when discovery is unified (SRV2-11).

title: Docker build is not reproducible and copies the wrong inputs
evidence: cargo build runs without --locked (Dockerfile:16, 23). tests/ is copied although the binary build never uses it (Dockerfile:20), which invalidates the layer cache. examples/ is not copied (Dockerfile:40), although /api/source and the demos expect ./examples (server.rs:122-123, 209-210).
impact: The lockfile can drift inside images, rebuilds are slower, and source lookups break in containers.
recommendation: Use cargo build --release --locked --bin openheart, drop COPY tests, and either copy examples or explicitly exclude it, with a documented runtime layout.

title: Launchers open the browser too early, run debug builds and lose fallbacks
evidence: run.sh opens the browser after 1 s (run.sh:33) and run.bat opens it immediately (run.bat:21), while cargo run may still be compiling for minutes. Both use the dev profile (run.sh:34, run.bat:22). If the build fails, exec cargo run (run.sh:34) and goto :eof (run.bat:23) skip the Python fallback.
impact: First-run users see connection errors, get a slower server, and have no fallback when the build fails.
recommendation: Run cargo build --release first and fall back on failure. Poll /api/health before opening the browser, then exec the release binary.

title: Direct-file fallback cannot load the module-based studio
evidence: When neither cargo nor Python is found, run.sh:52-54 and run.bat:51-55 open web/index.html via file://. The page uses ES modules (script type=module, web/index.html:408) and fetches diagrams/*.json, and Chromium browsers block both for file:// origins.
impact: The last-resort launcher shows a broken or empty studio.
recommendation: Open the hosted Pages URL instead, or ship a non-module bundle for file:// use, and print a clear message.

title: run.bat batch-parsing hazards: unescaped ')' in a block, delayed expansion
evidence: Inside the 'where py ... && ( ... )' block, line 36 echoes 'Python launcher (py) detected'. Its unescaped ')' closes the block early, leaving a syntax error once execution reaches line 35. setlocal enabledelayedexpansion (run.bat:2) is unused, but it corrupts paths containing '!' in cd /d "%~dp0" (run.bat:15).
impact: Systems with only the py launcher, or repo paths containing '!', get batch errors instead of the studio.
recommendation: Escape the parentheses as ^(py^), drop enabledelayedexpansion, and test the script with each interpreter combination.

title: run.bat trusts 'where python', which finds the Microsoft Store stub
evidence: run.bat:27 and 43 accept any python or python3 on PATH. On Windows 10/11 without Python, the WindowsApps execution alias is found, python -m http.server exits with 'Python was not found', and goto :eof (run.bat:32) ends the script before the py and direct-browser fallbacks.
impact: Users without Python get nothing instead of the documented fallbacks.
recommendation: Probe with python -c "import sys" and check errorlevel before choosing a branch, and fall through on failure.

title: run.bat is checked out with LF line endings
evidence: .gitattributes:2 forces '* text=auto eol=lf' with no override for *.bat, and the working copy of run.bat contains only LF (checked with od). cmd.exe parses LF-only batch files unreliably, especially label scanning and block parsing.
impact: Windows checkouts can hit intermittent batch failures that are hard to diagnose.
recommendation: Add '*.bat text eol=crlf' and '*.cmd text eol=crlf' to .gitattributes and renormalize.

title: Python fallback listens on all interfaces and assumes Python 3.7+
evidence: python -m http.server PORT --directory web (run.sh:49; run.bat:31, 39, 47) binds every interface by default. --directory needs Python 3.7+, 'python' can be Python 2 on older systems, and the version is never checked.
impact: The studio is exposed to the LAN, and older interpreters fail with an argument error.
recommendation: Add --bind 127.0.0.1 and check the interpreter version before launching.

title: restart_server.sh misreports when lsof is missing and runs a debug build
evidence: '2>/dev/null || true' hides a missing lsof (restart_server.sh:11), so the script prints 'No existing server process found' and then cargo fails to bind. The script is Unix-only, yet the Makefile targets call it on every platform (Makefile:39-44). It runs cargo run (debug) with an unquoted ${PORT} (line 21).
impact: Diagnostics are misleading, the server runs slower, and make fails on Windows.
recommendation: Check command -v lsof (fall back to ss or fuser), quote variables, and run the release binary.

title: Hand-rolled server JSON breaks on error text and control characters, and session temp directories leak
evidence: Error responses splice messages into JSON without escaping (server.rs:529-533, 543, 550-553, 601). Ingestion errors embed `{:?}`-formatted paths that contain quotes and backslashes (ingestion/mod.rs:52,54), and lines 496-502 insert target_dir.display(), derived from the attacker-chosen repo name, unescaped. escape_json_str (701-707) handles only backslash, double quote, newline, carriage return and tab, so any other control character in a file name corrupts success responses too. The early returns at 527-605 skip remove_dir_all (693), leaking one openheart_sess_* directory per failed request.
impact: Clients get JSON parse errors instead of diagnostics, and repeated failing requests gradually fill the temp volume.
recommendation: Build every response with serde_json::json! (already a dependency) and a typed error body. Hold the session directory in a tempfile::TempDir (move tempfile out of dev-dependencies) so that every exit path cleans up, and cap total temp usage per job.

title: No caching validators or compression
evidence: serve_file and respond_json send no ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control or Content-Encoding headers (server.rs:305-307, 326-328). index.html (79 KB), style.css (42 KB) and large analyze JSON are re-sent uncompressed on every load.
impact: Page loads are slower and transfers larger on a server that is already single-threaded.
recommendation: Add ETag and Last-Modified with 304 handling, set Cache-Control per asset class, and gzip responses above a size threshold when Accept-Encoding allows.

title: HTTP server and git shell-out compiled into the library crate
evidence: lib.rs:1 exports pub mod adapters (server and web_repo), and Cargo.toml defines no features. Every library consumer therefore compiles an HTTP server that spawns git and writes to CWD-relative directories.
impact: Embedders who only need the analysis engine get a larger attack surface and longer builds.
recommendation: Move the server into the binary crate, or put it behind an optional 'server' cargo feature.

title: No request logging or structured observability
evidence: Only ad-hoc println! lines exist (server.rs:35-38, 314, 384), and they bypass the project logger and its levels. There is no per-request line with method, path, status and latency, no request id and no metrics.
impact: Incidents and abuse are hard to diagnose.
recommendation: Log one structured line per request through the logger, and add request ids and an optional metrics endpoint.

title: No graceful shutdown
evidence: start() loops over incoming() forever (server.rs:40-43), with no signal handling or stop flag. SIGTERM or Ctrl-C kills the process mid-clone or mid-write, leaving partial clones, temp dirs and half-written web/diagrams files (fs::write is not atomic, server.rs:671-689).
impact: Cache and output state can be corrupt after a restart.
recommendation: Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM: stop accepting, then finish or abort jobs cleanly. Write outputs to a temp file and rename.

title: No result cache: identical requests rerun the whole pipeline
evidence: Even when ./target_repos/<name> already exists, every request reruns Phases 1-9 and all exporters (server.rs:505-691). Nothing is keyed by commit SHA or source tree hash.
impact: Each repeat view of the same repository costs seconds to minutes.
recommendation: Cache results keyed by repository, commit, engine version and options, and serve the cached JSON and diagrams.
